title: Cities turning climate ambition into action: Climate Budget Summit
content:
The Climate Budget Summit at the EU Regions Week in Brussels brought city leaders, climate experts, and local practitioners to explore how municipalities can turn ambitious climate goals into concrete investments and measurable actions.

The Summit on 14 October 2026 was launched by the Climate-4-CAST project (co-funded by the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme and contributing to thw EUSBSR Policy Area Energy Actions) to emphasise the role of climate budgeting in helping cities align their financial decisions with climate neutrality objectives.

Organised as a partner event of the EU Week of Regions and Cities, it hosted ca. 50 participants sharing experiences and reflecting on practical solutions for including climate considerations in budgeting and governance. The discussion touched upon common challenges, such as how to manage competing priorities, limited resources and political realities. Most participants represented European local and regional authorities, alongside representatives from the European Commission’s DG REGIO, the Interreg Baltic Sea Region Programme, and the city networks Eurocities, ICLEI and UBC.

title: Five communities around Lobeke National Park set up and mapping!
content:
Since the last post we’ve conducted two fieldwork trips to Lobeke National Park. Fair to say it’s pretty out of the way – three days by 4X4 on mud roads ridden with muddy ravines in the rainy season and clouds of dust in the dry. But for this reason the area is pretty special, monkeys playing and peering down at you even in villages and around the base camp, gorillas commonly spotted along the tracks of forest, elephants meandering around as they please.

The abundance of animals and tight controls on community activities through the conservation service has however certainly created problems – local communities and particularly the Indigenous Baka hunter-gatherers have great fear of entering the forest due to rangers on patrol and so do not have access to the quantity and diversity of forest produce they rely on. That the farmed food that they are now increasingly encouraged to produce is regularly ravaged by monkeys, gorillas, porcupines and elephants leaves them trapped with little ability to get the nutrition they need.

title: Syria's New Reconstruction Fund a Chance for Reform
content:
Syria and the World Bank Group announced on October 18 the creation of the Syria Recovery and Reconstruction Trust Fund, known as START. Run by the World Bank, the fund will pool donor money and private investment to help restore infrastructure and public services, strengthen state institutions, and finance reforms the Syrian government identifies as priorities.

The World Bank estimates Syria’s post-conflict reconstruction will cost about US$216 billion.

Norway pledged approximately 90 million krone ($9.6 million) and the Netherlands €15 million ($16.8 million). START’s initial focus, according to Syria’s state news agency, SANA, is infrastructure, health and education. It will operate under World Bank policies, which include standards on stakeholder engagement, land acquisition, and grievance mechanisms. But those standards only cover START-funded projects and governance arrangements are still being finalized, according to SANA.

title: OPINION: Protecting the Sacred City of Anuradhapura
content:
By Dr. Asoka Bandarage*

COLOMBO. Sri Lanka | 27 October 2026 (IDN) — Buddhism was first introduced to Sri Lanka in Anuradhapura in the 3rd century BCE by Arahant Mahinda, the son of the Indian Emperor Asoka. For nearly 1500 years, Anuradhapura remained Sri Lanka’s capital and the intellectual and spiritual centre of Theravada Buddhism in Asia. The Anuradhapura civilisation achieved unmatched advances in architecture, engineering and urban planning, still evident in its monumental stupas, monasteries, palaces and sophisticated hydraulic and agricultural systems.

Buddhism was gradually assimilated into Hinduism and had disappeared from India by the 12th century CE. The Chola invasion from India and the sacking and conquest in 1017 CE dealt a heavy blow to Buddhist civilisation, ending Anuradhapura’s role as the island’s political capital. The sacred city has continued to face attacks, including the LTTE massacre of 146 devotees at the Sri Maha Bodhi on Vesak full moon, 14 May 1985. Yet Anuradhapura has survived as one of the world’s oldest continuously inhabited cities and as a sacred site that has attracted Buddhist pilgrims over the centuries.

content:
Visitors who came to the open house at the Physical Archive in Richmond, California, on October 20 were curious. They wanted to learn about the range of items collected, the process of preservation, and the staff responsible for making it all happen. 

As people toured the space and observed the various media being saved, many also expressed support and reverence for the Internet Archive’s work to provide universal access to all knowledge.

“I really care about preservation and digital culture. Places like this are important to maintaining and building the society we want to live in,” said Sidney Le, a film archivist who now works in logistics, of his third visit to the Physical Archives. “It’s good to see that people here are taking seriously the idea of holding on to culture and preserving it.”

Liz Rosenberg, donations manager for the Archive, welcomed the crowd in Richmond and provided directions for the evening.

title: Joint Statement by KR21, ALLEA, LIBER and SPARC Europe: Why Splitting Open Access from the ERA Act Would Cost Researchers
content:
While momentum seems to be building towards the introduction of a Secondary Publication Right (SPR) in EU law, a critical question remains: under which legal framework will this happen?

For years, preparatory work had been taking place as part of the European Research Area (ERA) Policy Agenda, overseen by the part of the European Commission’s Directorate-General for Research and Innovation. This led to well-evidenced reports on the legal barriers to accessing and sharing research, as well as an exploration of the impacts of different potential solutions.

However, in recent months, the suggestion has emerged that rather than being included in the forthcoming ERA Act, SPR should instead be part of a potential copyright reform to be launched in 2027.

This raises concerns. Separating an SPR from efforts to strengthen Open Access mandates risks leaving researchers in a difficult situation, caught between funder expectations, publisher requirements, and limited resources to pay Article Processing Charges. While ‘transformative’ agreements sometimes cover both publication and access costs, these are widely seen as unsustainable.

title: Afgaaninaisen katse: Pelko kasvaa Kabulissa, kun Taliban pidättää naisia huiveista huolimatta
content:
Kabul on naisille pelon kaupunki. Olivatpa he menossa lääkäriin, kauppaan tai tapaamaan sukulaisiaan, perille pääsy on epävarmaa.

He pelkäävät tarkistuspisteitä, talibanien moraalipoliiseja ja pidätetyksi tulemista väärän vaatetuksen tai miespuolisen saattajan puutteen vuoksi.

Monelle naiselle kotoa ulos lähteminen on vaikea päätös. He joutuvat pohtimaan, mitä tapahtuu, jos heidät pidätetään: Pääsenkö palaamaan kotiin? Jos pääsen, onko minulla vielä sama asema perheessä tai yhteisössä?

Syyskuussa talibanien moraalipoliisi pidätti Yhdysvalloissa toimivan afganistanilaisen Amu TV:n mukaan ainakin parikymmentä naista ja tyttöä Taimanissa Kabulissa.

Muutamat heistä kertoivat tulleensa pidätetyiksi, vaikka heillä oli määräysten mukainen päähuivi, hijab, ja poliisin repineen naisten vaatteita näiden päältä kahakassa. Yön yli jatkuneen pidätyksen jälkeen heidät vapautettiin vasta, kun perheet ja paikallisyhteisöt maksoivat takuut.

Ahmad (nimi muutettu) on katukauppias Taimanissa. Hän kuvailee pidätystä:

title: Ei vain kuultavaksi – kohti aitoa osallistamista
content:
Tulevaisuudessa elävien ihmisten mielipiteiden tulisi olla keskeisessä roolissa päätöksenteossa, kun kestävää tulevaisuutta rakennetaan. On selvää, että syntymättömien ihmisten osallistaminen ei ole mahdollista, mutta mielipiteitä täynnä olevia nuoria on paljon.

Nuoria tarvitaan mukaan laajasti koko päätöksenteon kentälle – mutta miten? Yksi selkeä tapa edesauttaa nuorten osallisuutta on tarjota heille enemmän tietoa heidän vaikuttamismahdollisuuksistaan. Tiedon tarjoaminen voi tapahtua esimerkiksi kouluissa, harrastuksissa, nuorisotiloissa tai sosiaalisen median välityksellä. Toisaalta some voi olla itsessään myös hyvä kanava osallistaa nuoria esimerkiksi kyselyiden avulla.

Nuorilla tulee olla arjen asiat kunnossa, jotta he pystyvät toimimaan merkittävässä roolissaan kestävyyssiirtymän toteuttajina. Maaseutupolitiikan KERÄ-verkosto korostaa tulevien eduskuntavaalien alla, että nuorten mahdollisuudet kestävään arkeen, koulutukseen, työhön, asumiseen ja harrastuksiin on turvattava myös maaseudulla. Nuorten yhdenvertaisista mahdollisuuksista huolehtiminen onkin keskeinen osa kestävän tulevaisuuden rakentamista.

title: A Reason for Optimism on US Competition Policy
content:
Mozilla has long called for US antitrust reform in digital markets. After several false starts, real change has yet to materialize. In the meantime, dominant tech players have further entrenched their hold, limiting choice and degrading people’s experiences. Integration of new AI services into existing ecosystems is enabling those same companies to perpetuate and accelerate that power.

But, there’s reason for optimism. Momentum is again building toward antitrust reform, and this time feels different. With support from start ups, middle tech challengers, civil society, and think tanks across the political spectrum – and most importantly, legislative champions in Congress – it’s clear that the time is coming.

This is a debate about how the largest tech companies control the products and innovations in the market, and access to the services the people use every day. At the center are questions about user choice, interoperability, privacy, security and whether independent innovators have an opportunity to compete on merit.

title: Turbulent Times Call For Experimental Law
content:
MUNICH — Shortly after wandering into the Munich Urban Colab this summer, I found myself trying to follow an intense conversation in German about the city’s new experiment with autonomous buses. A local official, clocking my curious puzzlement, offered an aside in English: “We are asking ourselves: ‘What does it mean when the law is an experiment too?’”

No question may be more essential to governance in our era of dangerous uncertainty. 

Global warming is accelerating faster than global treaties on mitigation can be negotiated. Climate catastrophes occur with a sudden ferocity beyond what current adaptation laws anticipate. Biological threats surface and kill before public health responses can be formulated. And AI is evolving faster and more wildly than regulators or lawmakers, or even its designers, expect.

All this dizzying unpredictability is undermining traditional legal structures. The threat is not just to the rule of law, but to the very nature of law, at least as humans have conceived it.

title: ‘Is This Real?’: A Serbian Investigative Journalist Reflects on the Country’s Stunning Election
content:
Sunday’s election marked a turning point in Serbia, with the ruling SNS party of Aleksandar Vučić handed a resounding defeat by a student movement that capitalized on mounting public anger over years of corruption and criminality.

Many of those abuses had been exposed by KRIK, an award-winning Serbian investigative outlet and OCCRP partner that has spent years covering the country’s criminals, its corrupt officials, and the connections between them. In return, its young journalists have withstood pressure most people can scarcely imagine: personal attacks by pro-government tabloids, an endless stream of lawsuits, and even death threats.

Now, a new era is dawning. The seemingly unbreakable control exercised by Vučić — who served as information minister under dictator Slobodan Milošević — has been broken.

In this interview, KRIK editor-in-chief Stevan Dojčinović reflects on what the last few days have meant for him, how the students did it, and what challenges lie ahead. As he spoke with OCCRP late at night, the sounds of celebration filtered in from the street.

This interview has been edited for length and clarity.

title: How Balzac’s Extreme Coffee Habit Fueled His Productive Writing Routine
content: Even now, in this age when the very reading of literature is endangered — or so the articles tell us — Honoré de Balzac (1799–1850) retains a notable ability to pick up new admirers. But even though he may have a decent readership by the standards of French novelists who died in the middle of the nineteenth century, one does wonder whether he still inspires the kind of devotion embodied by William Hobart Royce. A Brooklyn bookseller’s assistant first introduced to Les Cent Contes drolatiques as an impressionable (and duly scandalized) teenager on a trip to England, Royce became not just the early twentieth century’s foremost American expert on Balzac, but also a kind of clone of the man himself, right down to his appearance.

title: This Oil Company Is Linked to 1,000 Pollution Incidents and Other Violations. Oklahoma Never Punished It.
content:
In June 2023, staff at an Oklahoma regulatory agency were fed up. The state isn’t known for cracking down on oil and gas companies for polluting the environment, but for over a year, the staff had been building a case to punish Citation Oil & Gas, one of the nation’s largest privately owned oil companies. 

About 30 miles north of the Texas border, toxic wastewater was gushing from the ground outside the small city of Ardmore. In the mile-wide oil field known as the Bayou, an oily sheen glistened on creeks and long streaks of salt scarred the land. The so-called purges, bubbling up among stands of oak and walnut trees, also threatened drinking water sources, drawing attention from the Environmental Protection Agency, according to a federal report.

State investigators pinned the blame on Citation’s injection wells, which pump wastewater from oil production back underground at high pressures and volumes in order to produce more oil. But this injection came with risks.

title: Suomen Arkkitehtiliiton asiantuntijalausunto: RTS 26:25 Asuntoyhtiön linjasaneeraushanke
content:
Suomen Arkkitehtiliitto kiittää mahdollisuudesta lausua asuntoyhtiön linjasaneeraushanketta käsittelevästä ohjekorttiehdotuksesta. Ohjekortissa on esitetty kattavasti ja selkeästi linjasaneeraushankkeen eteneminen ja vastuut teknisestä näkökulmasta. Linjasaneeraushankkeeseen voi kuitenkin liittyä merkittäviä rakennussuojelukysymyksiä. Lisäksi rakennuksissa voi olla merkittäviä arkkitehtonisia arvoja, vaikka niillä ei olisi suojelumerkintää.

Linjasaneeraushanke koskee tyypillisesti rakennusten sisäpuolisia osia, jolloin merkittävimmät rakennussuojelukysymykset koskevat useimmissa tapauksissa porrashuoneita ja niihin kohdistuvia muutoksia. Tulevaisuudessa linjasaneeraushankkeissa saatetaan toteuttaa myös esimerkiksi paikallista energiantuotantoa, kuten katolle sijoitettavia aurinkopaneeleja. Tällöin linjasaneeraushakkeen suojeluharkinta voi koskea myös esimerkiksi vesikattoa ja julkisivun osia. Rakennushistoriaselvitys on hyvä työkalu arvojen selvittämiseen ja siinä voidaan keskittyä hankkeen ja rakennuksen kannalta keskeisiin kysymyksiin. Näin hankkeen tavoitteet ja reunaehdot ovat selvät kaikille osapuolille hankkeen alusta alkaen sujuvoittaen hankkeen toteutusta kokonaisuutena.

title: Seuran jäsen, hae mukaan työryhmien toimintaan!
content:
Työryhmätoiminta on Kirjastoseuran suola!

Etsimme nyt työryhmiin uusia jäseniä kaudelle 2027–28. Suomen kirjastoseurassa toimii vuonna 2026 kuusi työryhmää. Työryhmiin voit tutustua täällä. Lisätietoja työryhmien toiminnasta saat kunkin ryhmän puheenjohtajalta.

Työryhmiin etsitään jälleen uusia jäseniä. Samalla lomakkeella haetaan sekä työryhmän varsinaiseksi että opiskelijajäseneksi. Huomaathan, että koulutus-ja tutkimustyöryhmän suuren koon vuoksi ryhmään ei valita tällä hakukierroksella täysin uusia edustajia.

Työryhmätoiminta tarjoaa seuran jäsenille mahdollisuuksia verkostoitua, oppia ja kehittää asiantuntijuuttaan. Se tarjoaa vaikuttamiskanavan (suomalaiseen) kirjastotyöhön, auttaa tutustumaan kirjastokenttään valtakunnallisesti ja ryhmässä toimimisesta saa työtodistuksen. Käytännön toimintaan ryhmät saavat apua ja tukea myös seuran toimistolta.

Työryhmän tehtäviä ovat:

  • toimia Kirjastoseuran hallituksen tukena antaen asiantuntija-apua
  • edistää yhdenvertaisuutta ja moninaisuutta kirjastoalalla
  • tukea ammattitaitoa järjestämällä koulutuspäiviä ja ammattitapaamisia sekä tarjoamalla mahdollisuuksia vertaistukeen

title: Planerar du en gruppresa inom utbildning eller ett språkmöte?
content:
Tack till alla som i år sökt bidrag för studieresor i grupp inom utbildningssektorn eller för språkmöten. Ni var så många och era ansökningar var så bra att våra budgetmedel nu är slut. Vi har därför tillfälligt stängt de här två ansökningarna.

Varje år i oktober gör vi en budget för alla våra nästan 50 olika bidragsformer. Då uppskattar vi bland annat hur mycket ni kommer att ansöka om inom varje bidragsform under det kommande året. Våra uppskattningar baserar vi bland annat på hur mycket ni tidigare år ansökt om, olika satsningar inom varje sektor och mera allmänna lägesbedömningar.

I viss mån kan vi under året justera budgeten, men i bland får vi så pass mycket ansökningar inom en bidragsform att pengarna vi budgeterat helt enkelt tar slut innan året är slut.

Det här är nu läget för två av våra mycket populära bidragsformer med fri ansökningstid:

  • studieresor i grupp inom utbildningsssektorn och
  • Hallå! Språkmöten

    • Vi har i år fått så pass många och bra ansökningar inom de här bidragsformerna att vi redan delat ut hela vårt budgeterade belopp för 2026.

title: AI sell-off would rattle global economy, EU watchdog warns
content:
PARIS — Investors piling into a small number of mega technology companies could have a “significant impact” on the economy if the artificial intelligence bet doesn’t pay off, the head of the EU’s financial markets watchdog said.

Verena Ross, who is set to step down as chair of the European Securities and Markets Authority at the end of October, said in an interview that the “significant concentration of market value” in a few companies “raises some questions around how to ensure proper diversification of investor portfolios.”

Ross was speaking the day after American AI giant Anthropic filed paperwork to take the company public in what could be the biggest listing in history, but also a test of investor confidence in the current AI boom. title: AI bots flooded 2023 UK government consultation on disposable vapes ban
content:
Three-quarters of all responses were machine-generated in failed attempt to stop bill from passing into law, research finds

AI bots flooded a government consultation with tens of thousands of fake responses in a failed attempt to stop the UK’s ban on disposable vapes.

Three-quarters of all the responses to the 2023 consultation on the tobacco and vapes bill were machine-generated, in what is thought to be the first coordinated attempt to use AI to derail health policymaking in the UK.

title: Serbia’s leaderless student movement has won a historic election – but what happens next?
content:
Serbia’s leaderless anti-corruption coalition, the Student List, defeated the group led by former president Aleksandar Vučić’s Serbian Progressive Party (SNS) by a comfortable margin in October 25 elections.

Their 53.3% of the vote should get them 141 seats in parliament, well clear of the 125 seats needed to form a majority. The SNS can be a loud but ineffectual opposition with the 103 seats netted by their 39.7% of the vote.

The result was known shortly after polls closed, with Vučić conceding defeat 90 minutes later. Once the celebrations settle down, it looks as if Serbia will manage a peaceful transfer of power to a democratically elected government.

Read more: ‘We changed the system’: how Serbian students ended Alexander Vučić’s 12 years in power

This was not inevitable. By mid-afternoon on election day, news outlets were reporting concentrations of armoured police vehicles and movements of personnel at various spots in central Belgrade.

title: Putin hopes hardship will force Ukrainians to sue for peace – polling suggests it won’t work
content:
Vladimir Putin has a theory of victory in Ukraine.

It’s not the Russian president’s first theory – that was a quick, dayslong campaign – nor his second or third, which involved different land offensives in the east that quickly petered out. Instead, Putin’s latest hypothesis is that the relentless bombing of Ukrainian cities will impose so much hardship on civilians that they will concede to Russia’s war aims.

Yet, as experts on conflict and public opinion, we believe there is a significant problem with this idea. Chiefly, extensive academic research shows that airpower alone rarely achieves decisive political goals.

Bombs terrorize civilians, but our survey findings in Ukraine suggest they don’t change war outcome preferences. Indeed, recent data shows that suffering from power outages and wartime stress in Ukraine has no relationship to support for territorial concessions to Putin.

The targeting of Ukraine infrastructure has been part of Russia’s way of war since the invasion of February 2022.
snippet: Vladimir Putin has a theory of victory in Ukraine.
creator: John O’Loughlin, College Professor of Distinction in Geography and Fellow, Institute of Behavioral Science, University of Colorado Boulder

Kampanjan aikana kerätään myös varoja väkivallan vastaiseen työhön. Oranssit päivät alkavat kansainvälisenä naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan vastaisena päivänä 25.11. ja loppuvat ihmisoikeuksien päivänä 10.12.

Vuosittain merkittäviä rakennuksia valaistaan oranssiksi naisiin kohdistuvan väkivallan esiin tuomiseksi. Vuonna 2025 tiedossamme oli yli 200 valaistua kohdetta ja tapahtumaa ainakin 70 paikkakunnalla.  Mitä useampia rakennuksia, kirjastoja tai muita kohteita saamme mukaan kampanjaamme, sitä enemmän huomiota saamme meitä kaikkia koskettavalle aiheelle. title: Antitheodicy – A New Direction in the Philosophy of Religion?
content:
For a long time, antitheodicy remained a relatively marginal approach to the problem of evil and suffering. Over the past decade, however, significant new philosophical and theological contributions have been published. Understood not merely as a critique of specific theodicies but as a rejection of the entire project of theodicy, antitheodicy is increasingly recognized as one of the central frameworks for addressing suffering in the philosophy of religion, particularly with regard to the meaningfulness or meaninglessness of suffering.

This workshop aims to take stock of the directions antitheodicist research has taken and to consider the prospects it may open for the philosophy of religion. The workshop is open to all interested parties, but is required by November 16.

Thursday 26 November

Kielikeskus (Language center, Fabianinkatu 26), V5 sh 144

14:30 Welcome Address

Paper Session I. Chair: Sami Pihlström

14:45-15:45 Claudia Welz. Reasons for Having No Reason to Defend God (Version 2.0): Antitheodicy-Arguments in Kant, Kierkegaard, Wiesel, and Levinas.

15:45-16:45 Gabriel Echazú. Theodicy as Newspeak.

title: Wie Julian als Wikipedianer eine gefährdete Sprache schützt
content:
Ich bin im Februar 2004 zur deutschsprachigen Wikipedia gekommen, da war ich 15 Jahre alt. Als Schüler auf der Suche nach Informationen war ich natürlich auch Teil der klassischen Zielgruppe. Ich war sehr jung und mitteilungsbedürftig (lacht). Ich glaube, es gab damals um die 50.000 Artikel – da war vieles einfach noch nicht da und konnte noch beschrieben werden. Daher habe ich zunächst vor allem Artikel zu regionalen Themen aus Bautzen und der Oberlausitz bearbeitet. Seit 2005 bin ich außerdem Administrator in der deutschsprachigen Wikipedia.

Die obersorbische Wikipedia hat inzwischen mehr als 14.000 Artikel. Unter allen 348 Sprachversionen liegt sie damit auf dem 160. Platz, direkt vor Färöisch. Sie hat monatlich etwa 200.000 Zugriffe. Anlässlich des Geburtstags waren es im Oktober sogar über 800.000.

Ich war tatsächlich eher zufällig dabei, als die sorbische Wikipedia gegründet wurde. Das war bei einem Wikipedia-Tag am 2. Oktober 2006 in Dresden. Ich konnte damals noch gar kein Sorbisch. Ich habe zunächst eher auf der technischen Seite mitgearbeitet und Stück für Stück sorbisch gelernt. Erst 2010 oder 2011 habe ich mich dann getraut, auf Sorbisch zu schreiben.

title: När byggnaderna försvinner finns bilderna kvar
content:
Foto: Andrew4you, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons

Den 30 september avslutades årets svenska upplaga av Wiki Loves Monuments, en av världens största fototävlingar. Under en månad har fotografer i hela landet laddat upp bilder av byggnader, fornlämningar och miljöer som berättar vår gemensamma historia. Alla bilder är fritt licensierade och kan användas av vem som helst, till exempel på Wikipedia, i utbildning, i forskning eller av media. 

Under september laddades 1 332 bilder upp i den svenska tävlingen. Allt från Björkviks och Kumlaby kyrkor till miljöerna kring Långasjö finns nu fritt tillgängliga på Wikimedia Commons.

I Sverige kan man tävla med bilder av skyddade byggnader, kulturreservat, fornlämningar, k-märkta fartyg och båtar samt arbetslivsmuseer. Bilderna behöver inte vara tagna i september, utan det räcker att de laddades upp under september. Nu arbetar juryn med att välja ut de tio bästa bilderna, som går vidare till den internationella finalen. Vinnarna presenteras i november.

title: Fingo peräänkuuluttaa: ”Tässä historian taitekohdassa Suomen kannattaa katsoa neljää vuotta pidemmälle”
content:
Valtiovarainministeriön julkaisemat säästöehdotukset pitävät sisällään merkittäviä leikkauksia varsinaiseen kehitysyhteistyöhön tai jopa sen lakkauttamisen. Vaikka kehitysyhteistyön ensisijaisena päämääränä on köyhyyden ja eriarvoisuuden vähentäminen, se on myös Suomen taloudellisten etujen mukaista.

Jaa

Maailmassa, jossa valtiot kilpailevat kumppanuuksista nopeasti kasvavien maiden kanssa, Suomen ei kannata vapaaehtoisesti purkaa vuosikymmenten aikana rakennettuja suhteitaan kehittyvien valtioiden kanssa, muistuttaa suomalaisten kehitysjärjestöjen kattojärjestö Fingo.

Talouskasvu on tulevaisuudessa nopeinta globaalissa etelässä koko maailman mittakaavassa. Kansainvälisen valuuttarahasto IMF:n mukaan monissa Euroopan maissa kasvu jää vuonna 2031 noin yhden prosentin tasolle, kun taas Afrikassa vain harvan valtion talouskasvu jää alle kolmen prosentin. Esimerkiksi Etiopiassa talouskasvu on tulevina vuosina jopa 7–9 prosenttia.

Suunta ei ole muuttumassa tulevaisuudessakaan. Yli 85 prosenttia maailman väestöstä asuu ja kaksi kolmesta valtiosta sijaitsee globaalissa etelässä. Toisin sanoen: kehittyvien maiden merkitys kasvaa niin taloudessa kuin kansainvälisessä politiikassa.

title: Babe, wake up, press freedom is in danger!
content: What happened: The Czech right-wing populist government, led by billionaire prime minister Andrej Babiš, wants to fundamentally change the country's public media, trying to abolish the licence fee paid directly by citizens and instead fund Czech TV and radio from the state budget. Babiš's government pushed its proposal through a first reading in parliament in a rather shady way. They fast-tracked the parliamentary debate and scheduled the first round of voting at 4.36 in the morning on Saturday last week. Not exactly a common procedure for voting on something this big. It's almost... hmm... as if they tried to get away with something without much public attention. When word spread, spontaneous protest filled the square next to the parliament building throughout the night. The government majority passed the proposal anyway. In 2025, Babiš's ANO party campaigned on the reform, arguing that abolishing licence fees, which currently amount to CZK 205, or €8 per month, would relieve citizens. title: Exiled Russian Musicians Fill Arenas to Inspire the Lost Generation
content:
Hundreds of thousands of Russians have left their homeland since 2022, and among them are artists who publicly condemn the full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Despite being labeled foreign agents and prohibited from re-entering Russia, they keep playing shows in Asia, Europe, and North America.

As anti-war Russians in exile search for new cultural identities beyond Putin’s regime, the concerts serve as rallying points for their country’s lost generation.

Yelizaveta Gyrdymova, known by her stage name Monetochka, is at the forefront of Russian artists speaking out against the war. Banned from returning to Moscow, Monetochka continues touring abroad , where her performances attract thousands of diaspora Russians.

In her recent releases, such as “Это было в России” (It was In Russia), she evokes strong feelings of nostalgia in her audience by recalling fond everyday memories from the country she loves but is no longer allowed to call home.

title: Marissa Mayer Can’t Keep Pretending 'Gender Doesn't Matter'
content:
In Sunday’s edition of the New York Times, Marissa Mayer, former president and CEO of Yahoo, told her interviewer something so absurd it’s since gone viral. 

Struggling with the “impossible task” of naming three things that she loves about her own 10 year old daughter, the New York Times reports, Mayer asked the AI assistant she just launched to do that thinking for her. It delivered the perfect answer, Mayer said: “It came back and was like, your daughter is empathetic, creative and an animal lover.” Everyone is piling onto that absurd anecdote right now, rightfully so. What she has to say about gender in tech, however, is more out of touch than that.

title: Sri Lanka: Outrageous organized crime bill granting authorities unchecked powers must be withdrawn
content:
A new bill before Sri Lanka’s parliament that grants the authorities sweeping arbitrary powers to tackle ‘organized crime’ and deny suspects’ human rights should be immediately withdrawn, Amnesty International said today. 

The Prevention of Organised Crimes bill, tabled in Sri Lanka’s parliament on 6 October, contains provisions that would make confessions extracted under duress admissible in court, enable the detention of suspects for up to two years without trial, and ban the media from reporting on court proceedings. The bill also confers the police with wide powers to conduct searches without a warrant, and imprison people for not providing information to authorities.  

The bill mirrors many elements of Sri Lanka’s repressive Prevention of Terrorism Act (PTA), which has been misused since the 1970s to target minorities and repress dissent. 

“This extraordinary bill is the most alarming in a string of repressive laws proposed by the National People’s Power (NPP) government. It reintroduces most of the very worst elements of the PTA and applies them to a wide range of offences,” said Smriti Singh, Amnesty International’s South Asia Director.

title: Guest post: Greenland ice sheet shrinks for 30th year in a row
content:
• Surface mass balance
  • Total mass balance
  • Surface melt
  • Snowfall
  • Iceberg calving 
  • The impact of global weather
  • Three decades of decline
  • Greenland in the global sea level picture

    • Greenland has now marked the 30th consecutive year where it lost more ice than it gained. 

    This guest post is by:

    Dr Martin Stendel, climate scientist at the Danish Meteorological Institute (DMI), part of the Polar Portal 

    Prof Ruth Mottram, climate scientist at DMI and honorary professor at Aarhus University

    Over the 12-month period to August 2026, the world’s second-largest ice sheet lost around 135bn tonnes of ice. 

    This major ice loss came as the region experienced a relatively cool start to summer and less surface melt than in previous years. 

    In other words, it was not an “extreme” year for weather in Greenland – and, yet, the ice sheet ended firmly in the red.

    Three decades of continuous ice loss in Greenland is significant, given that scientists typically need 30 years of data to separate the “fingerprint” of human-caused climate change from natural variations in the climate. 

    In Greenland, the direction of travel has been the same – downward – every single year for 30 years.

title: "Anti-Fascist Economics": Isabella Weber on How Inequality Fuels Extremism & Erodes Democracy
content:
With the U.S. midterm elections just a week away, the affordability crisis — intensified by President Trump’s tariffs and war on Iran — has emerged as a major campaign issue. Across the country, families are struggling to make ends meet, while oil and gas companies have reported record profits during recent periods of price shocks.

Economist Isabella Weber’s new book, Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability, Dignity, and Democracy, warns economic insecurity can fuel the rise of authoritarian movements, and argues protecting democracy requires making life affordable for everybody.

Anti-fascist economics is “not about getting rid of the market,” says Weber. “It’s about having public players that behave differently, and by behaving differently, changing the dynamic of the market as a whole and literally creating an alternative so that people are not dependent on often very concentrated and private providers as the only choice,” she explains, providing current examples of governments enacting such policies from New York City to Mexico City to Rome.

title: New Records Obtained by EFF Expose More Problems with Medicare’s AI Experiment
content:
New records obtained by EFF expose additional issues with Medicare’s AI-driven prior authorization program and show why we need stronger legal limits around government use of automated decision-making. 

EFF sued the government back in March for information about the Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction (WISeR) model, a new Medicare program that uses AI to evaluate prior authorization requests for certain medical services. We previously released records showing that WISeR has resulted in delays and denials of care, operational chaos, and reports of patient harm. Today, we’re publishing over 800 new pages of records, including:

  • Requests for information (RFIs) or requests for corrective action plans (CAPs) sent from the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) to four of the six WISeR vendors, along with the vendors’ responses.
  • Applications of 66 companies to the WISeR model, including those of the 6 selected companies. 
  • Task orders and contracts for the evaluation, implementation, and monitoring of the WISeR model.

    • Documents obtained through EFF’s lawsuit are available here.

title: Suomen lääkeala: Rakenne, kehitys ja taloudellinen merkitys
content:
Suomen lääkeala on kokoonsa nähden taloudellisesti poikkeuksellisen merkittävä toimiala. Ala työllistää alle prosentin yrityssektorin työvoimasta, mutta tuottaa lähes kymmenen prosenttia sen liikevoitoista. Vuosina 2008–2019 alan reaalinen arvonlisäys kasvoi noin 60 prosenttia samaan aikaan, kun koko yrityssektorin arvonlisäys laski, ja vuonna 2024 se oli edelleen tällä tasolla. Työn tuottavuus on yli kaksinkertainen yrityssektorin keskiarvoon verrattuna.

Lääkeala on myös poikkeuksellisen osaamisintensiivinen. Yli kolmannes henkilöstöstä on suorittanut ylemmän korkeakoulututkinnon ja lähes kaksi kolmesta toimii asiantuntija- tai johtotehtävissä. Viime vuosina alan vienti on kasvanut voimakkaasti erityisesti alkaloidipohjaisten lääkkeiden viennin vetämänä. Suomi on pitkällä aikavälillä pysynyt mukana globaalien lääketeollisuuden arvoketjujen kasvussa, vaikka sen suhteellinen osuus on viime vuosina hieman pienentynyt.

title: Egypt: Prominent Journalist Lina Attalah Detained
content:
(Beirut) - The New Cairo Misdemeanor Court convicted Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent news platform Mada Masr, of operating without a license in a single hearing on October 27, 2026. The court fined her 3 million Egyptian pounds (US$53,474) and ordered the website’s closure. The authorities took Attalah into custody after the hearing. Mada Masr reported that prior to ruling, the judge cleared the courtroom, rejected all procedural motions presented by Attalah’s defense team including requests to present evidence and hear from witnesses, and replaced her defense counsel against her will. 

Attalah had received a summons on October 19 to appear for questioning before the Supreme State Security Prosecution and Egyptian authorities on October 22 referred her to trial on charges of establishing, managing, and operating a website without a license.

title: 40 years in the spirit of Assisi
content:
By Benoit Lannoo*

ASSISI. Italy | 27 October 2026 (IDN) — Today, it has been exactly forty years since John Paul II brought together different religions in Assisi for the first time for an interreligious prayer for peace.

In his recently published book (in Italian, French and German) entitled Assisi – The Origins of a Spiritual Globalization, the Roman historian Andrea Riccardi, founder of the Community of Sant’Egidio, points out that even the “iconographic material of Assisi 1986” remains important. He is referring to the emblematic photo of St. Pope John Paul II surrounded by the Dalai Lama and a large number of other leaders of Churches and religions, sitting next to each other on small chairs all of the same size in the square in front of the lower basilica of St. Francis in Assisi. They had just prayed for peace at the same time but all in their tradition and customs.

Alas, for today’s closing ceremony of the 40th Meeting in the spirit of Assisi, the current pope will not be physically present since the doctors have advised him not to travel by helicopter. But Leo XIV will send a message to the festive assembly.

title: U.S. Court Sentences Lender to 15 Years over $76M Ponzi Scheme
content:
A U.S. federal court has sentenced a businessman to 15 years in prison for his role in running a Ponzi scheme that defrauded hundreds of investors out of millions of dollars. According to a statement from the Department of Justice, Edwin Brant Frost IV, the founder of a conservative, Christian lending firm in Georgia, defrauded more than 300 investors out of over $76 million in a massive Ponzi scheme. Frost, who was convicted of wire fraud in May after pleading guilty, will also have to pay back over $76 million in restitution to victims.

According to federal prosecutors, Frost's now-defunct company, First Liberty Building and Loan, LLC, ran the Ponzi scheme between at least 2021 and July 2025. Frost scammed investors by claiming he was making high-interest, short-term “bridge loans” to small businesses. Prosecutors stated that after most of the bridge loans defaulted, Frost began using new investor funds to pay interest to existing investors, while secretly diverting at least $5 million for lavish personal purchases and political contributions.

title: A Soviet Animation of Stephen King’s Short Story “Battleground” (1986)
content: Stephen King has that rare, and spectacularly profitable, skill to suck you into his world and compel you to flip to the next page. And when you’re hooked, his words have the uncanny ability to simply unfold like a movie in your head. So it isn’t surprising that his books have been widely adapted to the silver screen. Some are flat out masterpieces. Others are most decidedly not. This appreciation by filmmakers of King’s storytelling chops isn’t just contained to this side of the Iron Curtain. In 1986, Soviet animator Mikhail Titov — whose previous work includes How the Cossacks Played Football (1970) — turned King’s short story “Battleground” (1972) into an animated movie, titled simply Сражение or Battle.

Arvoisat puhemiehet, hyvät ministerit ja Pohjoismaisen neuvoston jäsenet, hyvät naiset ja herrat, hyvät pohjoismaiset ystävät!

title: Rakennusten purkaminen on kiihtynyt – SAFA esittää selvityshenkilöä
content:
Suomeen on syntynyt purkamista suosiva toimintakulttuuri, joka on haitallinen sekä ilmaston että rakennusperinnön kannalta. Selvityshenkilön tehtävänä olisi kartoittaa monitahoista ongelmaa sekä ratkaisuja siihen, miten Suomi voi siirtyä kohti korjaamista, uudelleenkäyttöä ja rakennusperinnön turvaamista.

Olemassa olevan rakennuskannan kohtelulla on ratkaiseva ja kauaskantoinen merkitys ilmaston, talouden, kulttuuriperinnön ja arkiympäristön kannalta.

”On kriittinen kysymys, miten rakennuskantaa korjataan, muutetaan ja puretaan. Korjausrakentamisen tukemisella olisi myös vahva työllistävä vaikutus”, SAFAn puheenjohtaja Asko Takala sanoo.

Tilastokeskuksen mukaan vuonna 2023 purettiin noin 8 000 rakennusta, mikä on kaksinkertainen määrä vuoteen 2010 verrattuna. Purettavaksi päätyy jopa arvokasta rakennusperintöä: 1930–1940-lukujen harvinaisia funkisrakennuksia, yli satavuotiaita hirsitaloja ja Suomen arvostetuimpien nykyarkkitehtien töitä. Esimerkiksi arkkitehti ja akateemikko Juha Leiviskän suunnittelema, vuonna 1983 valmistunut Kirkkonummen seurakuntakeskus on edelleen purku-uhan alla.

title: EU eyes global tax deal revenue to boost next budget
content:
BRUSSELS — The European Commission is exploring whether to use revenue from a global tax agreement on multinational companies to finance the EU’s next seven-year budget, four EU diplomats with knowledge of the proceedings told POLITICO.

The idea could facilitate an agreement on new EU-wide taxes, known as own resources, which has emerged as a major stumbling bloc in the ongoing budget negotiations.

The European Council President António Costa has urged countries to approve the new taxes to reduce national contributions to the bloc’s budget, which is worth €1.82 trillion according to the latest proposal from earlier this month.

Costa, who is brokering budget talks, is pressuring leaders to reach a budget deal among themselves by the end of the year — before elections in Poland, France and Italy threaten to derail the negotiations.

Yet after more than a year of haggling, EU governments are still at odds over five proposed new taxes that the Commission estimates would generate €65 billion per year.

title: Is France in 2026, Greece in 2009?
content:
France’s ten-year government bond yield reached 5% last week, its highest level in more than two decades. The extra interest it pays over Germany – the “spread” investors use to gauge French-specific risk – has widened dramatically. Parliament is wrestling with a 2027 budget requiring €54 billion in fiscal measures, while protests and violent clashes across France dominate the headlines.

With political instability and social tensions rising, comparisons with Greece at the start of its debt crisis have become inevitable. As Greece’s finance minister when its crisis erupted in 2009, I am increasingly asked how the two situations compare. I understand the temptation, but also how misleading it can be.

France is not Greece. It is one of the world’s largest economies, with globally competitive companies, substantial household savings, a deep financial system, robust institutions. And, unlike Greece in 2009, it has no large external financing imbalance.

title: Anthropic’s record US$2 trillion stock market listing highlights the growing risks for all of us
content:
Anthropic, developer of AI chatbot Claude, has filed its prospectus and is expected to go public on Wall Street in November at a valuation of up to US$2 trillion.

That would make it the highest-valued initial public offering (IPO) ever, ahead of SpaceX’s US$1.77 trillion listing in June. OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT, is expected to follow next year.

While these AI-powered IPOs are massive, they reflect an ever bigger trend: holding AI risk is becoming unavoidable for most investors.

How much of your portfolio depends on how well AI does? If you invest in an S&P 500 index fund, the answer is about 44%.

In addition, most of the market’s gains right now come from AI. Just six companies – Apple, Microsoft, Meta and chipmakers Nvidia, Micron and AMD – delivered 57% of the S&P 500’s gains since April. Without them, the index would have risen about 4% rather than 10%.

For investors or even future retirees, that AI exposure is already in their portfolios and pension funds. For example, at the end of 2025 Australians held nearly A$1 trillion in US shares – through superannuation or pension funds, other managed funds, and their own investments.

title: Ulkomaalaistaustaisten uhrien pahoinpitelyt kasvoivat rikostilastoissa
content:
Viranomaisten tietoon tulleiden rikosten määrä kasvoi viime vuonna lähes 6 prosenttia, noin 553 500 kappaletta. Pahoinpitelyjen osalta viranomaiskirjaukset lisääntyivät jälleen, ja ulkomaalaistaustaisten uhrien osuus niissä nousi noin 7 prosenttia. Pahoinpitelyjen uhreista heitä oli 19 prosenttia vuonna 2025 ja 12 prosenttia vuonna 2016.

Yleisesti pahoinpitelyrikosten kasvua havaitaan erityisesti alle 18-vuotiaiden ja 30–50-vuotiaiden epäiltyjen kohdalla, mutta kyselytutkimusten perusteella väkivallan uhriksi joutuneiden osuus pysyi ennallaan.

Nuorten osalta pahoinpitelykirjausten kasvu heijastelee sekä lainsäädännön muutoksia, jotka vaikuttavat kirjaamiseen, että nuorten kasvanutta alttiutta ilmoittaa rikoksista, Helsingin yliopiston tiedotteessa arvioidaan.

Myös aikuisista yhtä moni kuin ennenkin kertoi kokeneensa fyysistä väkivaltaa, vaikka tilastoissa luvut kasvoivat.

title: Ett register för fria verk – nu är CommonsDB avslutat
content:
Målningen Frukost i det gröna av den svenske konstnären Carl Larsson. Public Domain


Hur vet man om en bild, en text eller ett musikstycke är fritt att använda? Under de senaste 18 månaderna har Wikimedia Sverige tillsammans med europeiska partner byggt en infrastruktur som skulle kunna ge  svar på den frågan. Nu är pilotprojektet CommonsDB avslutat.

När vi lanserade CommonsDB i mars 2025 var målet att ta fram en prototyp till ett offentligt register över verk som är fria att använda, alltså verk i public domain och verk med öppna licenser. I dag saknas en pålitlig plats där man kan kontrollera vad som gäller för ett visst verk. Det skapar osäkerhet för forskare, kulturarvsinstitutioner, AI-utvecklare och alla andra som vill återanvända material.

Projektet har drivits av Open Future tillsammans med Wikimedia Sverige, Europeana Foundation, Liccium och Institute for Information Law vid Amsterdams universitet, med finansiering från EU.

Registret fungerar, och det fungerar i stor skala. Det innehåller nu över 6,5 miljoner verifierade uppgifter om verks rättighetsstatus, vilket är över en miljon fler än projektet hade som mål.

title: Serbia is free
content: For most of my life, Serbia was a place that you'd better leave. And so I did. But last night, as I followed election results deep into the night all the way from the Netherlands, I felt that Serbia might be a place to come back to for perhaps the first time in my life. Around 21.30 on election night, former president Aleksandar Vučić conceded that his party SNS, which has been in power for the last 14 years, had lost to the Student List, born out of a protest movement that has shaken Serbia since November 2024. Almost instantly, “Serbia is free” echoed all over social media as city streets erupted in joy and celebration. The police, who had been blocking the street in front of the Republic Electoral Commission and patrolling Belgrade since the morning, began to retreat, and two years of building tension was released in fireworks, chants, and dancing deep into the night. The Student List won by a landslide. According to the Republic Electoral Commission, and based on 97% of counted votes, the Student List won 52.65% of the votes and is projected to gain 140 out of 250 parliamentary seats, enough for a parliamentary majority. title: Serbia’s New Government Has a Mountain to Climb
content:
There is something in the air in Central Europe, and it smells like change. After the landslide victory of Hungary’s Péter Magyar in April, the Student List ousted Serbia’s long-time strongman Aleksandar Vučić with a convincing electoral win on October 25.

Even so, it will prove difficult to relaunch the country’s democratization process and navigate international waters after 12 years of illiberal, Kremlin-friendly Vučić rule.

As with Viktor Orbán in Hungary, there had been much discussion of a Belarus-style theft of the result using the security forces to beat down the winners. As with Orbán, this did not happen. Instead, at around 9:30 p.m. on election night, Vučić took the stage and conceded defeat. He had lost by 53% to 39%, and his opponents had secured a working parliamentary majority from the highest turnout for 34 years.

Across Serbia, the initial shock was followed by wild celebrations that continued late into the night, and the capital city of Belgrade suddenly became a scene of public joy not seen since the ousting of the president and war criminal Slobodan Milošević in 2000, after he attempted to steal an election.

title: Trump Is Already Undermining Confidence in Midterm Election Results from Alaska to California: ACLU
content:
A competitive Senate race has gripped the once reliably Republican state of Alaska. If Democratic challenger Mary Peltola wins the election against incumbent Republican Senator Dan Sullivan, it could tip the balance of power in Washington. Attorneys for Peltola and the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee have submitted a motion to dismiss a Department of Justice lawsuit filed last week that seeks to block the certification of the election results in Alaska if Sullivan loses. President Trump confirmed on Friday he had ordered the DOJ to file the lawsuit, which alleges that the appearance of another candidate on the ballot with a similar name, Daniel J. Sullivan Jr., would mislead voters. The Alaska Supreme Court ruled ahead of the primary that Sullivan Jr., a retired schoolteacher who is running unaffiliated, could appear on the ballot.

The ACLU — on behalf of two Alaska voters, the League of Women Voters of Alaska and Common Cause — has moved to intervene in the case and has also filed a motion asking the court to dismiss it.

title: French Court’s Site-Blocking Orders Drive Quad9 Out Of France
content:
A nonprofit service that protects internet users’ privacy is leaving France. Quad9, a free DNS resolver, has said it will reluctantly stop serving users in France on November 24. This follows a French court order that Quad9 must block access to websites that are accused of infringing the copyrights of a sports broadcaster. Forcing a responsible privacy service out of an important market is a predictable result of trying to force infrastructure providers to be copyright police.

When you visit a website, a DNS resolver reads the domain name you type in—like eff.org— and translates it into a numerical IP address that’s used to direct data across the internet. A DNS resolver can see the names of websites you connect to, so its privacy policies are important. Quad9 is an NGO that’s incorporated in Switzerland, in part to protect its users from data demands. The company also helps protect users from malware and phishing by blocking domains that are known to be malicious. Services like Quad9 offer an alternative to the DNS resolvers of local internet service providers and wireless carriers, which are vulnerable to demands from law enforcement, censorship, and commercial surveillance.

title: Azerbaijan’s Hijab Restrictions Exclude Girls From School
content:
School officials across Azerbaijan have been turning away girls wearing hijabs following the introduction of new government dress regulations, sparking protests across the country. Police have detained dozens of people amid the protests, while Instagram and TikTok users have reported difficulties accessing the platforms as public criticism of the restrictions has grown.

Azerbaijan’s Cabinet of Ministers amended school uniform regulations on September 21, prohibiting clothing "inconsistent with the principle of secular education." Although the regulations do not explicitly mention hijabs, schools began refusing entry to girls wearing headscarfs when the rules took effect on October 12. News reports showed distressed girls after being turned away from schools.

Separate dress requirements adopted on October 6 also affected teachers.

title: Impatient with Brussels, European capitals forge ahead with social media bans
content:
Six weeks after the EU unveiled its much-anticipated proposal to protect kids across the bloc from social media, European governments are pressing ahead with their own rules. 

National political leaders had spent months asking for unified age restrictions for social media access across the European Union, to avoid 27 different sets of rules. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s response came in September with the EU Kids Act, a signature initiative of her second term that would ban under-13s from accessing most current social media platforms and severely restrict access for under-15s. 

But it is becoming clear that individual countries don’t want to wait for the Brussels legislative wheels to turn — and in some cases, are proceeding with national laws that would kick even more kids off the platforms than what von der Leyen has in mind.  

“While we wait for the EU Kids Act – we are pushing forward with national legislation,” Denmark’s digital minister Christina Egelund said. “The problems are urgent. Children and parents should not be asked to wait.”

title: The Black Sea is turning green, and not the good kind
content: “This summer, we went 38 km deep in the Black Sea. You can see how it is more green,” Martin Tomov, a campaigner for Greenpeace Bulgaria, told us. Satellite images from EUMETSAT confirm his observation. The scientific name for this is eutrophication: an excess of nutrients allows algae to bloom, turning rivers and seas from crystal blue to green. It happens when manure or nitrate- and phosphate-based fertilisers spread on farmland run off into rivers. When the algae later die and rot, they strip the water of oxygen, which suffocates fish, and can also release a poisonous gas. “They also block sunlight; it prevents many organisms from surviving, which impacts the entire food chain,” Tomov told us. In 2016, a jogger died on a beach in Brittany, France, after inhaling poisonous gas from rotten algae. A court held the state liable nine years later, and France compensated his family. But Europe is far from responding adequately. Nearly one third of the EU's rivers, lakes, and coastal waters, and 81% of marine waters, are eutrophic according to an EU report from early this year. title: Russia’s Drone Incursions Multiply in Moldova
content:
Russian drones have crossed into Moldovan airspace more frequently in 2026 than at any time since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine more than four years ago.

Chișinău International Airport has been forced to suspend operations for spells to protect civilian aviation, and Moldovan authorities have admitted that, while they can detect the drones, they lack the capacity to intercept them.

A French radar system bought with public money, and another with European Union assistance, sound the alarm, but Moldova does not have the resources for military jets or other systems to shoot them down.

Neighboring Romania has F-16 fighters, but Moldova cannot benefit from their support because its neutrality blocks such military cooperation.

The Air Operation Service of the national army reported at least 81 cases of Russian drone incursions in the past four years. The frequency of such incidents grew gradually from a few cases in 2022 to more than 40 so far this year. Six missiles have also been detected.

The majority were believed to be heading for targets in Ukraine and deviated into Moldovan airspace.

Authorities took Attalah into custody after the hearing before releasing her hours later following payment of the fine.

(Beirut) – Egyptian authorities should drop their case against Lina Attalah, editor-in-chief of the independent media outlet Mada Masr, ahead of her October 27, 2026 hearing, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Supreme State Security Prosecution (SSSP) referred Attalah for trial on October 22 in Case No. 9072/2026 on charges of establishing and managing a website without a license. She faces a fine of up to 3 million Egyptian pounds (about US$53,400) as well as the closure of Mada Masr and confiscation of its equipment.

title: Who’s who at the EU-Canada summit
content:
Brussels and Ottawa want to forge closer ties in an increasingly uncertain world. Meet the people shaping their partnership.

By ZOYA SHEFTALOVICH
and NICK TAYLOR-VAISEY

Photo-illustration by Gibson Kochanek for POLITICO

Brussels and Ottawa want to deepen their partnership at an Oct. 29-30 summit in Montreal, where Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney’s push for a middle-powers alliance will meet European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen’s bid for geopolitical influence.

The outcome may fall short of von der Leyen’s bold offer to make Canada an associate EU member, particularly as EU countries remain divided on the idea. But the push reflects a shared desire to reduce dependence on the U.S. and secure supply chains, with the two sides aiming for closer cooperation on energy, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, computing and financial services.

In a draft declaration, Canada and the EU also envisage “mutually favorable treatment” if they align their economic security policies — a nod to maintaining a united front amid the challenges posed by China.

title: Elon Musk’s AI Odyssey review – the dullest, most pointless riposte possible to Christopher Nolan’s brilliant epic
content:
It is hardly a shock that Grok AI’s interpretation of Homer is as meaningless as a laptop screensaver. The only surprise would be if Musk accepted defeat graciously. Which he won’t

Think back. Do you remember when Elon Musk, in a weird online tantrum, and without having seen the film, condemned the supposed wokery in Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey, for getting Elliot Page to play Sinon and Lupita Nyong’o to play Helen of Troy? As the plaudits and the box-office receipts for Nolan’s Odyssey piled stratospherically up, Musk showed that being a good loser is not among his qualities. He petulantly exclaimed that he could do his own better and more authentic Odyssey on Grok AI. And now he has released the first online seven-minute “episode” to a world that has long since forgotten about this claim and didn’t care in the first place.

title: Warmer seas and shifting pressure systems: the signs that suggest the Mediterranean’s climate is ‘tropicalising’
content:
Nowhere in the Iberian Peninsula or the Balearic Islands has a tropical climate – for this to be the case, the average temperature in the coldest month would have to be 18°C or higher. The contrast between Spain’s winters and summers, and the low temperatures reached in winter, do not resemble those of any tropical climate.

However, over recent decades, climates across Mediterranean basin have begun to show signs of tropicalisation: the process of transitioning towards a tropical climate.

This is evident in several areas, including rising air and sea temperatures, shifting atmospheric patterns, and increasingly erratic rainfall.

Firstly, a marked rise in air temperature – more pronounced than the global average – is making the Mediterranean’s winters shorter and its summers longer, bringing spring forward and delaying the onset of autumn. Some people believe that these transitional seasons have all but disappeared. They do still exist, but they have moved on the calendar.

The temperature of shallow and deep Mediterranean water – down to a depth of around 100m – has also risen markedly.

title: Mitä Jokeri ja Tyrion Lannister kertovat ihmisyydestä? Huumoria tutkiva Jarno Hietalahti syventyy Kaaos nauraa -teoksessa ilkikuristen hahmojen merkitykseen
content:
Triksterit ovat myyttisiä tai maagisia olentoja, jotka rikkovat rajoja velmuilla tavoilla. Huumorin filosofian dosentti Jarno Hietalahti tarkastelee kirjassaan Kaaos nauraa: Loki, Jokeri ja muita kujeilijoita myyteistä nykypäivään näitä häpeämättömiä ja ilkikurisia olentoja avaimina huumorin olemukseen. Ne kertovat meille ihmisyydestä ja elämästä sekä nostavat esiin huumorin suhteen moraaliin, politiikkaan ja hyviin tapoihin. Samalla triksterit muistuttavat, että kapealle maailmankuvalle on aina vaihtoehtoja.

Jos huumori olisi hahmo, miltä se näyttäisi? Pilkkaa ja huvituksia tarjoavat triksterit voidaan nähdä huumorin ruumiillistumina, jotka herättävät teoriat hauskuuden luonteesta eloon. Nämä mytologiset irvailijat ja kujeilijat viis veisaavat säännöistä, paljastavat piilotellut salaisuudet, haastavat auktoriteetteja ja aiheuttavat kaaosta.

title: EU divisions persist on ‘associate member’ label for Canada
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU was split Tuesday over whether to offer “associate membership” status to Canada, with several countries refusing to sign off on a statement containing that phrase just 48 hours before a summit between the two sides in Montreal.

After EU capitals could not agree on the language in the statement in talks between ambassadors Monday, they used the so-called silence procedure on Tuesday. That meant a new text would be adopted automatically without a formal meeting or vote, if no countries objected by midday.

But Germany, which is leading the push to have the term “associate member” fully removed from the text, was among at least four countries that broke the silence procedure before that deadline, said two EU diplomats, granted anonymity to speak freely. That means the topic will be discussed Wednesday at another meeting of EU ambassadors, just one day before the EU-Canada summit kicks off.

The fracture shows how divided the EU remains on the idea of “associate membership,” which European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen offered to Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney during her State of the Union speech in Strasbourg last month.

title: France: Lawmakers must reject regressive “Rioters Pay” bill
content:
France’s proposed bill to make demonstrators pay for damage caused to property by acts of violence in street protests, even if they did not directly cause it themselves, will have a chilling effect on freedom of peaceful assembly and must be rejected by lawmakers, Amnesty International said ahead of a two-day debate in the Senate. 

This bill threatens to further deter people from exercising their rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly 

Nathalie Godard, Amnesty International France

This bill threatens to further deter people from exercising their rights to freedom of expression and peaceful assembly 

If passed, the legislation commonly referred to as the “Rioters Pay” bill, could hold individuals liable for acts they did not personally commit, provided they ‘knowingly’ participated in a gathering where acts of violence, theft, destruction, or property damage took place. A protester could be liable to pay up to 10,000 euros; in addition, social benefits could be seized if compensation is not paid, which risks plunging already marginalised families further into poverty. Parents may also be held civilly liable for acts that their children did not commit.

content:
26.10.2026

    Doctor of Philosophy and Adjunct Professor Pasi Rautio has been appointed for the position of Professor in Arctic Resilience and Adaption at the Arctic Centre of University of Lapland. The Professorship also includes the tasks of the Director of the Arctic Centre for the term lasting until the end of 2029.

    Rautio will begin in his position on 11.1.2027. Currently he works as a Research Professor of Silviculture in the Natural Resources Institute Finland (Luke) in Rovaniemi. The new professorship is part of the University of Lapland’s strategic choice of Global Arctic responsibility.

    Rautio earned his Doctor of Philosophy in Plant ecology at the University of Oulu, where he also holds a docentship of Plant and Environmental Ecology. For a long time, Rautio has worked in research assignments at the Natural Resources Institute Finland and at its predecessor Finnish Forest Research Institute (METLA). In addition, he has worked at the European Commission in Brussels and been involved in numerous international research projects and international networks within his field.

title: BSR Cultural Pearls 2027: Applications Submitted, Cultural Pearls 2027 will be announced on 9 November
content:
The applications for BSR Cultural Pearls 2027 have been submitted, and the jury has begun its evaluation. The title recipients will be announced on 9 November 2026. Meanwhile, Cultural Pearls cities continue to bring communities together through cultural activities.

The past weeks have marked an important stage for BSR Cultural Pearls. Applications for the 2027 title have been submitted, and the international jury, comprising 11 members, has started evaluating the submitted Community Resilience Action Plans (CuReAPs). The applications reflect the participating municipalities’ approaches to addressing local challenges, strengthening community resilience and using culture to encourage citizen participation.

The new BSR Cultural Pearl will be announced on 9 November 2026, marking the next milestone in the programme. The selected municipality will join a growing network of towns and cities across the Baltic Sea Region that use culture as a means of fostering community engagement, dialogue and a sense of belonging.

An award ceremony is planned for 17 November in Glücksburg, as part of the first Future Cities Forum (16–18 November 2026).

title: Miten biisin saa radioon? Ammattilaiset paljastavat tärkeimmät vinkit
content:
Radio on edelleen yksi tehokkaimmista tavoista tavoittaa suomalaisia musiikin ystäviä, minkä takia monelle artistille radiosoitto voi olla merkittävä ponnahduslauta laajemman yleisön tietoisuuteen. Lisäksi radiosoitot kerryttävät äänitteille tekijänoikeuskorvauksia.

Mutta mitä musiikkipäälliköt ja musiikkitoimittajat oikeastaan etsivät uusista kappaleista? Ja miksi osa erinomaisistakin biiseistä jää soittolistojen ulkopuolelle?

Kokosimme yhteen tärkeimmät vinkit artisteille, tekijöille ja levy-yhtiöille.

Yksi yleisimmistä virheistä on alkaa rakentaa kappaletta liikaa radiosoitto mielessä. Alan ammattilaisten mukaan radiosoittoa ei kannata miettiä liikaa vielä tekovaiheessa.

Jos luovuus alkaa taipua liiaksi oletettujen radiosääntöjen mukaan, lopputulos voi menettää omaleimaisuutensa. Parhaat kappaleet syntyvät usein aidosta ideasta, tunteesta tai tarinasta.

Hyvä radiobiisi on lopulta monen asian summa.

”Siinä täytyy olla jotain, mikä herättää tunnetta ja resonoi yleisössä”, toteaa SuomiRäpin ja Basson kanavapäällikkö Riikka Karjalainen.

Radiosoittoon tarjottavien kappaleiden tulee täyttää tekniset laatukriteerit.

title: Yemen: Houthi Attack on Taizz Road Threatens Lives, Welfare
content:
(Beirut) – The Houthi armed group on October 18, 2026, used explosives to severely damage a critical road into Yemen’s besieged city of Taizz, putting civilian lives and welfare at increased risk, Human Rights Watch said today. 

The Hayjat al-Abd road has been the main entry point for food, medicine, and fuel to reach residents of Taizz city, which the Houthis have besieged since 2015. Fighting in the area has primarily been between the Houthis and forces aligned with Yemen’s internationally recognized government. The Houthis’ deliberate destruction of segments of the road, if intended to disable infrastructure indispensable to civilian survival, would violate the laws of war and amount to a war crime. The attack may also have caused disproportionate civilian harm.  

“The Houthi attack on the remaining commercial supply route to besieged Taizz further endangers civilians already struggling with severe shortages of food, water, medicine, and fuel,” said Niku Jafarnia, Yemen and Bahrain researcher at Human Rights Watch. “If Taizz residents’ access along this vital route is cut off for a prolonged period, they could face even greater risks to their lives and well-being.”

title: Improving Cities from Space: Geospatial Innovations in North and Central Asia
content:
By Kareff Rafisura, Ladislav Charouz and Elena A. Pronina*

BANGKOK | 26 October 2026 (IDN) — Cities in North and Central Asia are growing quickly, bringing them face to face with the interlinked challenges of rapid urbanisation, rising population density, and heightened vulnerability to disaster and climate risks. World Cities Day is a good opportunity to consider these challenges and how geospatial technologies can help address them.

Following up on an earlier ESCAP article about satellite-enabled urban solutions in East and North-East Asia, this piece turns to North and Central Asia, where governments are applying geospatial technologies and satellite data across a growing range of areas – from monitoring and urban planning to tracking accessibility.

Disaster and climate resilience is one such area. Kazakhstan, for example, uses a satellite monitoring system, JerScan, to keep track of ageing infrastructure, reducing the need for physical field inspections.

title: What role for cultural heritage institutions in the age of AI?
content:
Three recent initiatives address the role of the cultural heritage sector amid the rise of AI:

  • the European Commission’s call for evidence on the AI Strategy for the Cultural and Creative Sectors;
  • A European Parliament own-initiative report on the cultural and creative sectors in the age of AI; and
  • the policy paper entitled Beyond adopter and supplier: putting cultural heritage at the heart of Europe’s Public by the European Heritage Hub, an EU-funded project bringing together stakeholders from the cultural heritage sector.

    • All three initiatives rightly recognise the dual role of cultural heritage institutions as users of AI systems and providers of resources for AI development. They also raise valid concerns about the visibility and discoverability of Europe’s diverse cultural heritage and less-resourced languages. Yet only the European Heritage Hub’s policy paper and a handful of the 5,442 contributions to the call for evidence envision cultural heritage and other knowledge institutions as active participants in shaping a future with AI.

title: ”Mitä helvettiä teen täällä, kun täällä tarvitaan leipää ja teitä eikä mitään tanssia” – Bolivialaisen Pachi Sejasin ja Alpo Aaltokosken ystävyys rakentaa siltaa maanosien välille
content:
Pieni poika istuu tien varressa maitolaiturilla ja katsoo ohitseen kahteen suuntaan kulkevia autoja. Hän miettii, minne ne ovat menossa ja mistä tulossa. Mitä siellä jossain muualla on?

”Kasvoin pienessä Hiidenkylässä Pyhäjärven kunnassa Oulun alapuolella. Elinpiirini oli kirjaimellisesti kodin pihapiiri. Kuusivuotiaaksi asti se oli ainut maailma, jonka tunsin. Kauppakin oli monen kilometrin päässä”, sanoo tanssija-koreografi Alpo Aaltokoski, 68.

Sittemmin Aaltokoski on reviiriään kiitettävästi laajentanut, maita ja mantuja kiertänyt.

Nyt lokakuussa hän viettää Tanssin talossa 40 vuotta kestänyttä taiteellista uraansa. Kolmen soolon juhlassa kolme kansainvälistä naistanssijaa tulkitsee Aaltokosken sooloteokset Huominen ja Eilisen jälkeen ja Ethno Contemporary Ballet -ryhmän teoksen Fertility.

Ohjelma heijastelee Aaltokosken pitkäkestoista kulttuurivaihtoa ja laaja-alaista esiintymistoimintaa myös Suomen rajojen ulkopuolella.

Jo 1990-luvulta alkaen Aaltokoski on rakentanut verkostoja erityisesti Latinalaiseen Amerikkaan. Yhteistyö alkoi Nicaraguasta ja jatkui myöhemmin Meksikoon ja Boliviaan.

title: Ukrainan ulkoministeri Sybiha ja Norjan ulkoministeri Eide vierailevat Helsingissä
content:
Ukrainan ulkoministeri Andrii Sybiha ja Norjan ulkoministeri Espen Barth Eide vierailevat Helsingissä ja tapaavat ulkoministeri Elina Valtosen 27. lokakuuta. Suomen, Ukrainan ja Norjan ulkoministerit tapaavat myös kolmenvälisesti. Tapaamisen aiheena on Ukrainan rauhanprosessi.

Ulkoministerit Valtonen ja Sybiha keskustelevat muun muassa Suomen ja Ukrainan kahdenvälisistä suhteista, Suomen tuesta Ukrainalle ja Ukrainan polusta kohti jäsenyyttä Euroopan unionissa.

”Ukraina puolustaa Venäjän hyökkäyssotaa vastaan taistellessaan koko Euroopan turvallisuutta. Olemme juuri lisänneet merkittävästi tukeamme Ukrainalle sen valmistautuessa vaikeaan talveen. Maittemme tiiviit suhteet vahvistuvat myös yritysten yhteistyön kautta”, ulkoministeri Valtonen toteaa.

Yhteisessä tapaamisessaan ulkoministerit Valtonen, Sybiha ja Eide keskustelevat rauhanprosessin tilanteesta ja seuraavista askeleista kohti rauhaa. Rauhanneuvottelujenkin rinnalla on yhä tärkeä jatkaa vahvaa tukea Ukrainalle ja painetta Venäjälle. 

”Suomi ja Norja ovat Ukrainan läheisiä kumppaneita ja vahvoja tukijoita. Teemme yhdessä väsymättömästi työtä sen eteen, että Ukrainaan saadaan kestävä ja oikeudenmukainen rauha.”  Valtonen jatkaa.

title: Today: the latest in our FOI webinars
content:
Dear friend,

Just a reminder that this free online webinar is happening today at 15:00 UK time. Do join us: if you're able: it's set to be a very interesting session!
 

We can’t take our Freedom of Information laws for granted — as we’ve seen through the years with governmental pushback both in the UK, and in countless countries around the world.

In this free webinar, we’ll hear from those at the frontline of defending the right to know in Germany and Mexico, two countries where recent changes have raised important questions about the future of Access to Information.

In Germany, FragDenStaat say that they are facing "the most serious attack on transparency in the history of the Federal Republic and a threat to our democracy", with a proposed scrapping of ATI. In Mexico, a change in the agency responsible for FOI has undermined public access to information, ruling against most requests.

We hope you’ll join us today to hear these fascinating stories, and what civil society is doing to kick back against such challenges: find out more and book here.

Veza is Strategic Campaigner at FragDenStaat (Ask the State) in Germany.

title: ‘Students Have Won’: Overwhelming Turnout Shatters Serbia’s Entrenched Regime
content:
When a handful of university students first spilled onto the streets two years ago to protest the deadly collapse of a railway station canopy, Serbia’s state-run media dismissed them as unruly kids merely looking for an excuse to cut class.

They were grieving the 16 people crushed to death and demanding accountability for what they condemned as lethal state corruption and crony contracting, bearing banners that read: “Corruption kills” and “Your hands are bloody.”

But those scattered demonstrations soon swelled into a generational revolt. Over two relentless years, the students slept in occupied lecture halls, barnstormed rural strongholds where state television branded them foreign mercenaries, and punctured a pervasive climate of fear with biting wit and viral banners.

On Sunday, the kids actually did it.

In a stunning ballot-box upset that shattered Aleksandar Vučić’s 14-year grip on power, Serbia’s student-led movement defeated the Balkan country’s formidable ruling machine, clinching a triumph so historic that even its young architects were left reeling in disbelief.

title: Harry Houdini Died 100 Years Ago This Halloween: Was He Really Killed by a Punch to the Stomach?
content: This Halloween marks the 100th anniversary of the death of famed escape artist Harry Houdini. Today, most of us know more about the manner of that death than we do about any of the feats of escape artistry that made him famous in the first place. As the story goes, he’d mastered his own body to the extent that he could tighten his abdominal muscles so as to withstand even the hardest punch to the gut. Or at least that’s the image he let circulate: taking it as a challenge, a student and amateur boxer turned up and offered his fist to Houdini as an unexpected test. A week and a half later, the great escapologist was dead of peritonitis.

title: Ministerien erityisavustajat muodostavat uuden poliittisen vallan kerrostuman
content:
Kriisit ovat vahvistaneet erityisavustajien asemaa, ja osa heistä rakentaa jo omaa poliittista profiiliaan julkisuudessa. Muutos herättää perustavan kysymyksen: kuka käyttää valtaa – ja kuka siitä lopulta vastaa?

Pääministeri Sanna Marinin entisen erityisavustajan Tuulia Pitkäsen kynästä ilmestyi hiljattain kirja, joka lupaa johdattaa lukijan yhteiskunnallisen päätöksenteon saloihin, kiemuroihin ja kihelmöiviin hetkiin.

Politiikan tutkijalle Tuulia Pitkäsen kirjan julkaiseminen on itsessään mielenkiintoisempi ilmiö kuin kirjan varsinainen sisältö. Sitran vanhempi neuvonantaja Taru Turunen toteaakin arviossaan, että kirjaa vaivaa innokkuudestaan huolimatta kritiikittömyys, joka ei tarjoa uutta analyysia puolueiden tulevaisuuden ja naisen ja vallan kytköksestä.

Viime aikoina onkin nähty viitteitä siitä, että avustajien omalla nimellä antamat haastattelut olisivat yleistymässä. Yle teki viime vuonna henkilöjutun valtiovarainministeri Riikka Purran talouspoliittisesta erityisavustajasta Jussi Lindgrenistä ja vuotta aiemmin Purran viestintäavustajasta Matias Turkkilasta.

Vuonna 1944 julkaistussa kirjassaan The Children of Light and the Children of Darkness (Valon lapset ja pimeyden lapset) Reinhard Niebuhr tutkii demokratian ja ihmisluonnon välistä perusjännitettä. Lempisitaattini kirjasta on ”Ihmisen kyky toimia oikeudenmukaisesti tekee demokratian mahdolliseksi, mutta ihmisen taipumus toimia epäoikeudenmukaisesti tekee demokratiasta välttämättömän”. Luin kirjan ensimmäisen kerran perustutkinto-opiskelijana Furman-yliopistossa Yhdysvalloissa. Kuvaavaa kyllä, teos kuului amerikkalaista poliittista ajattelua käsittelevän kurssin lukemistoon.

title: In a Newly Drawn District, Black Voters May Get a Representative Who Spent Years Undermining Their Interests
content:
Not two weeks after the Tennessee legislature carved Memphis into three congressional districts this spring, in a move designed to eliminate Democratic representation, Republican state Sen. Brent Taylor made his electoral expectations clear in a photo posted on social media. 

Taylor and U.S. Rep. Tim Burchett, a fellow Republican, sat side by side on the U.S. Capitol steps. “My friend Tim Burchett showing me the dadgum ropes,” Taylor wrote in a Facebook post.

On May 7, the same day that the new districts were approved, Taylor had announced his bid to represent the redrawn Congressional District 9, which for more than four decades had stood as the state’s sole majority Black district. During that time, it covered mostly the Memphis area; it now stretches across half the state and is majority white.
