title: The Nordic-Baltic Eight policy brief: China’s green statecraft and NB8 Arctic security
content:
NB8 Policy brief -sarjan uusi julkaisu, kirjoittajat Dana Dūda (LIIA), Konstantinas Andrijauskas (IIRPS VU) ja Björn Cappelin (UI).

Energy dependence has become a geopolitical liability. Russia’s war against Ukraine, the US-Iran war and tensions with the Kingdom of Denmark over Greenland have all exposed the strategic weight of energy independence, critical minerals, and Arctic access. For the eight Nordic-Baltic states (NB8), the next vulnerability may emerge from the green transition itself, where China’s dominance in clean technologies and critical mineral processing can be converted into strategic leverage. Some dependence is unavoidable in the short term; the task is to manage it deliberately rather than let it accumulate by default. This policy brief argues for integrating green energy security and Arctic security within a one strategic framework, because the Arctic’s critical mineral resources, renewable energy infrastructure and emerging transport and digital connectivity projects are relevant to Europe’s efforts to strengthen its energy dependence. This brief proposes collective measures to limit strategic dependence on China in the long term.

title: Kuilu nais- ja miesvaltaisten alojen työelämän laadussa kasvanut hallituskaudella
content:
Suomen Ammattiliittojen Keskusjärjestön (SAK) uusi seurantatutkimus osoittaa, että työelämän laatu on heikentynyt naisvaltaisilla aloilla, kun taas miesvaltaisilla aloilla se on palannut lähelle huipputasoa. Erot ovat kasvaneet voimakkaasti Petteri Orpon hallituksen kaudella.

SAK:n julkaisema Hyvän työn mittari seuraa työelämän laatua keskusjärjestön kattamilla aloilla, joista suurimpia ovat teollisuus, yksityinen palveluala (esimerkiksi kaupat) ja julkinen sektori. Mittarin mukaan elpyminen vuoden 2024 notkahduksesta on tapahtunut vain osittain, ja nousu on ollut eritahtista eri toimialoilla. Selvimmin on elpynyt teollisuuden työntekijöiden työelämän laatu.

SAK:n mittaushistorian pahin kuoppa työelämän laadussa näkyi vuosien 2022–2024 luvuissa, jolloin laadultaan huonon työn osuus kasvoi järjestön aloilla kuudesta prosentista kymmeneen.

Naisvaltaisilla julkisilla palvelualoilla työelämän laatu on heikentynyt edelleen vuodesta 2024. Yksityisillä palvelualoilla 35 prosenttia työntekijöistä on laadultaan huonossa työssä. Julkisilla palvelualoilla huonon työn osuus on 25 prosenttia, mikä on sekin historiallisen korkea tulos. Laatua mitataan kymmenellä eri mittarilla.

title: Extremists have no idea what Norse mythology is really about
content: Thor, the Norse god of thunder, once visited the giant Utgard-Loki. The giant challenged him to empty a drinking horn, lift a cat, and wrestle an old woman. He failed all three and left questioning his power. As it turned out, Utgard-Loki had used magic to hide Thor's real opponents. He had been drinking from the ocean, and the cat was Jörmungandr, the gigantic sea serpent encircling the earth. The old lady? Old age itself. This is the Norse myth I remember most clearly. For most people across Scandinavia and Iceland, the old myths don’t play a big role in everyday life, but there are subtle signs of them. Weekdays, streets, and people are named after Norse gods, for instance. Or the countless TV shows, comics, books, and music inspired by old gods and myths. We don't know when and how Norse mythology started, but it was definitely practised in Scandinavia and Iceland in the late Iron Age (from 500 AD) and Viking Age (800-1050 AD). Northern Europe was then gradually Christianised around the year 1000, through missionaries and due to pressure from foreign trade from the south. title: Saamelaisneuvosto jakoi Dalán-avustuksia
How the Philadelphia Museum of Art Brought 600 Teen Voices Into Its American Art Galleries
content:
How do you make a major gallery reinstallation feel relevant to young people who may never have visited your museum? The Philadelphia Museum of Art answered that question with a simple tool: a postcard. Its teen programs team distributed more than 2,000 blank postcards to local teens and collected over 600 drawings back for display in the museum.

The drawings were prompted by two short instructional videos, each led by a Philadelphia teaching artist and rooted in themes from the museum’s reinstalled American art galleries. The result was a teen community engagement project that combined real curatorial depth with wide community reach, and brought new families through the museum’s doors.

The museum reinstalled its American art galleries to mark the semiquincentennial, the 250th anniversary of the United States. The new presentation, A Nation of Artists, asks a pointed question: who gets to be an American artist?

Följ med på en musikalisk resa mellan Finland och Sverige! Konserten På tonernas brygga utforskar hur dikter från Finland landstigit hos svenska och nordiska tonsättare och hur Finlands främsta musikskapare tonsatt svensk lyrik – från både Finland och Sverige. Studerande och lärare från Sibelius-Akademin i Helsingfors gästar Finlandsinstitutet med sånger från olika tider i en skön blandning av stilar.

Vi hör allt från urgamla koraler och tidiga pionjärer som Bernhard Henrik Crusell, till älskade klassiker av nationalromantiker som Jean Sibelius, Armas Järnefelt och Selim Palmgren. Kvällen bjuder också på vår tids musik av tonsättare som Carita Holmström och Sebastian Fagerlund.

Musiken och urvalet presenteras under konsertens gång av Gustav Djupsjöbacka i samtal med Finlandsinstitutets direktör Wivan Nygård-Fagerudd.

För sången står sopranerna Alvilda Elmarsdóttir, Hanna Hasu och Inka Österberg samt barytonen Petteri Salomaa. Vid flygeln sitter Gustav Djupsjöbacka och David Szilasi.

title: Complementary forces: Why activism needs art to drive action
content:
‘A striking action, a touch of humor, or an unexpected scene can attract attention.’

Originally published on Global Voices

An urban art piece called “The Post is fast, it's only the letters that arrive slowly” in front of the main Post Office in Skopje, North Macedonia.

This post is by Nikola Pisarev, an art historian and a pioneer of creative activism in North Macedonia, who serves as the program director at the Contemporary Art Center in Skopje. It is also part of Global Voices’ September 2026 Spotlight series, “Protest in Democracy.” You can support this coverage by donating here.

In recent decades, practices that bring art directly into people’s everyday lives have become increasingly common. They may be initiated by artists, activists, informal groups, or citizens who use creative means to draw attention to a problem, express disagreement, or call for change. Public spaces become a place where an action meets an audience, provokes a response, and starts a conversation. This approach, when artistic and creative means are used to press for solutions or encourage social change, is called artistic activism.

title: The Right Thing to Do: How Openness Supports Research Integrity
content:
The theme of International Open Access Week this year is the cost of knowledge. This shines a light both on the major contributions made by the research sector itself (and how these are then captured by private actors) and on the lack of transparency around costs in the publishing field. 

One argument made to justify the continued use of paywalls and high fees for article processing is that this helps to maintain the infrastructure for safeguarding scientific integrity, from peer review to editorial checks and the handling of misconduct. Without these business models, the story goes, these services can no longer be provided. Yet given how little transparency there is on publishing costs, it is rarely clear how much of what institutions and funders pay actually goes towards integrity.

Integrity is indeed a major issue. It is essential not only to maintain the quality of science, but also to safeguard the trust of the public and funders. Stories of malpractice damage confidence in research as a whole. 

The question then is whether closing access (either to reading through subscription fees, or to publishing through article processing charges) is an acceptable ‘sacrifice’.

title: Many in Serbia’s Youth Movement Fear a Rigged Election on Sunday
content:
Riding an extraordinary wave of public mobilization, Serbia’s student-led opposition heads into Sunday’s snap parliamentary election genuinely believing it can break President Aleksandar Vučić’s 14-year grip on power.

Yet beneath the euphoria of this week’s mass rallies lies a pervasive conviction among its supporters that the contest will be anything but fair—and that the ruling party will resort to outright ballot theft rather than concede defeat.

On Thursday night, that tension was on full display as hundreds of thousands of people flooded into Belgrade’s central Slavija Square, filling the surrounding boulevards in a buoyant, flag-waving display of collective defiance. The assembly marked the movement's final campaign rally ahead of an early vote that serves as the culmination of nearly two years of youth-led unrest against Vučić’s rule.

What began in November 2024 as grief and outrage following the collapse of a newly renovated railway station canopy in the northern city of Novi Sad—a disaster that killed 16 people and was turned by the protesting youth into a lethal symbol of state corruption and crony contracting—has since metastasized into a nationwide rebellion.

title: Ken Paxton Says He’s Tough on Crime. His Trust Invested $600,000 in a Convicted Fraudster’s Company.
content:
Four years after North Texas home builder Scott Sherman completed a federal prison sentence for mortgage fraud, his new construction materials business received a $600,000 cash infusion.

The financial boost came from a blind trust set up to prevent Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton and his wife, state Sen. Angela Paxton, from any overlap in their personal investments and their actions as elected officials. But previously unreleased records from the attorney general’s 2023 impeachment investigation show the trust was far from blind and did not shield the Paxtons from its business dealings, including the investment in Sherman’s business.

Before long, Wildcatter Sand Services and Grayson County Sand and Gravel, which Sherman built with his father, grew into a vast enterprise with various locations and subsidiaries. And along the way, some of those businesses stopped paying taxes to local governments, including school districts.

title: Starlink still restricted for Ukraine despite Trump saying Musk lifted speed limits
content:
KYIV — Ukrainian interceptors still cannot use the internet at high speed to shoot down Russian attack drones or conduct mid-strike operations as of Friday morning, Ukrainian officials and a drone operator said, despite U.S. President Donald Trump saying SpaceX founder Elon Musk had lifted speed restrictions on his Starshield service.

“Morning tests show the speed limits of 140–160 km/h are still there, and the navigation isn’t working properly,” a Ukrainian government official told POLITICO on condition of anonymity.

“As of this morning, instances of connectivity loss at speeds of 161 km/h are still being observed. There is currently no confirmation that the restrictions have been lifted,” a defense ministry official told reporters on Friday.

Ukrainian drone units started testing speed limits from Thursday evening, shortly after Trump told reporters that Musk had restored Starlink. While some tests recorded speeds of up to 200 km/h over the Black Sea and noted an improvement, the drones still rapidly lost signal once flying above the 160 km/h speed limit.

title: Experts cast doubt on Anthropic report detailing how AI has altered work at the company
content:
Anthropic claims AI will shift how work gets done and labor demand – but some experts are skeptical of the vision

Last year, the Anthropic CEO, Dario Amodei, warned that artificial intelligence could eliminate half of entry-level white-collar jobs and that in six months it would be writing 90% of code. Neither of those predictions came to pass.

Now, in a report Anthropic published on Thursday, the company said it was hiring fewer junior technical workers and that human attention has become the new “bottleneck” as it increasingly relies on its Claude AI agents.

title: The Crucible: Arthur Miller’s morality tale was as much a reaction to his own marital failings as it was to the ‘red scare’
content:
Written at the height of the cold war “red scare”, Arthur Miller’s 1952 play The Crucible was a retelling of the 17th-century Salem witch trials (1692-93) which soon became the classic parable of mass hysteria.

Miller’s play has long been described as “a cornerstone of American theatre” and “an allegory of our times”. Adapted into a 1996 Oscar-nominated Hollywood film, recent stage revivals on Broadway (2016) and at the UK’s National Theatre (2022) further confirm its enduring popularity.

A staple of the high-school syllabus (a YouTube search yields over 3,200 school productions), the play has also come to shape popular understandings of early modern witchcraft. As Miller (1915-2005) foresaw, its interpretation of Salem became a flexible model applicable to other tragedies – so flexible, in fact, that “witch-hunt” has in recent years devolved into a virtually meaningless political catchphrase.

title: Vihreiden Forsgrén vaatii ministeri Rydmanilta selvitystä paperittomien terveysneuvonnan päättymisestä
content:
Lääkärien sosiaalinen vastuu ry, LSV, on saanut ennakkotiedon paperittomuustyönsä STEA-rahoituksen päättymisestä ensi vuonna. Järjestön mukaan ennakkotiedossa vedotaan sosiaali- ja terveysministeri Wille Rydmanin toiveeseen. Asiasta kertoi Lääkärilehti 20. lokakuuta.

Kansanedustaja Bella Forsgrénin mukaan ministerin on kerrottava, pitääkö tieto paikkansa ja millä perusteilla rahoitusta ollaan lopettamassa.

"Ministerin henkilökohtaiset mieltymykset eivät saa ratkaista, ketä Suomessa autetaan", Forsgrén sanoo vihreiden tiedotteessa.

LSV on lähes kymmenen vuoden ajan ohjannut paperittomia ihmisiä terveydenhuollon piiriin, neuvonut heitä hoito-oikeuksista ja kouluttanut terveydenhuollon ammattilaisia. Järjestön mukaan kahden asiantuntijan työ maksaa 140 000 euroa vuodessa. Ilman rahoitusta neuvonta ja kohtaava työ loppuvat.

"Olen järkyttynyt. Puhumme työstä, jonka ansiosta diabeetikko saa insuliinireseptinsä, toistuvasti kouristeleva lapsi pääsee tutkimuksiin ja odottava äiti neuvolaan. Hinnan maksavat ihmisten terveys ja päivystykset, joihin hoitamattomat sairaudet lopulta päätyvät", Forsgrén sanoo.

title: What does the C say about your yoghurt?
content: Let's say you're in a shop looking for yoghurt. You're standing at the fridge, choosing between strawberry and plain. The pots show five letters, running from a dark-green A to a red E. The one you're holding has a C. Hmmm. Those letters are the Nutri-Score, a label weighing sugars, saturated fat, salt, and calories against fibre, protein, and the content of fruit, vegetables and legumes in products per 100 g or 100 ml. The label was first adopted in France in 2017 and has since been picked up in Germany, Belgium, Luxembourg, Switzerland, the Netherlands, and Spain. International supermarkets have also brought it elsewhere, which is why you'll see the label on Lidl shelves in Latvia, for example. Using it is voluntary for producers. We analysed nearly one million EU-listed packaged products with a Nutri-Score in the Open Food Facts database from all over Europe, and found that nearly three-quarters (73.9%) were rated C, D, or E. Does that mean nearly three-quarters of these products are unhealthy? The answer isn't straightforward. title: What the Saint Louis Art Museum Learned from Four Bold Audience Experiments
content:
What happens when a museum invites babies, dogs and stand-up comedians through its doors? At the Saint Louis Art Museum (SLAM), it became a two-year testing ground for museum audience development. Educators Jessica M. Kennedy, Erica Richard and MaryClaire Pavlick shared four of these experiments at MuseumNext: what they tried, what worked, what didn’t and what they learned along the way.

SLAM was founded in 1879 and now holds more than 38,000 works spanning five millennia and six continents. Its home, the Palace of Fine Arts, displayed 11,000 works during the 1904 World’s Fair. For more than 115 years the museum has offered free admission, and “Dedicated to Art and Free to All” is carved above its main entrance.

The museum serves a region of nearly three million people across Missouri and Illinois. Most visitors come from the City of St. Louis and St. Louis County, whose tax support makes free admission possible.

Yet free entry alone does not make everyone feel welcome. That gap is what led SLAM to the Access for All grant.

title: Ohio Governor's Race: Trump Backs Ramaswamy Ad Siding with Opponent's Indicted Childhood Rapist
content:
President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance have both defended Ohio gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy after his campaign released a TV ad that appears to accuse Democratic nominee Amy Acton of lying about being sexually abused as a child. Acton’s stepfather was indicted in 1978 on charges of sexually assaulting her when she was between 10 and 12 years old, though he fled before he could be convicted. Acton’s mother, who lost custody of her two children, sided with her husband and remained with him as a fugitive until his death in 2004. In the controversial campaign ad, the elderly Donna Arthur says her daughter Amy has “lied her entire life” and can’t be trusted as governor, which has been widely interpreted as casting doubt on what Acton has said about being abused as a minor.

“Vivek Ramaswamy is now using that personal trauma as an effort to exploit what she went through and win this race,” says Abby Vesoulis, a reporter for Mother Jones. “He’s currently polling beneath Amy Acton, which shows, I think, that this ad is a desperate attempt to somehow pull off a victory despite poor odds.”

title: Sanctioned Investor in Cambodian Scam Compound Owns California Mansion
content:
Brendon Luo was sanctioned in June by the U.S. Treasury Department, which alleged he was an investor in a cyber-scam compound operated by Cambodia's Prince Group. Property records show he still owns a mansion in a gated community in southern California.

The Prince Group is widely accused of involvement in compounds in Cambodia where thousands of trafficked workers were forced to commit industrial-scale cyberfraud. The Prince Group has strongly denied the accusations, but the U.S. has sanctioned more than 140 allegedly-associated entities and individuals, including Luo.

The sanctions have not disrupted Luo’s ownership of a five bedroom mansion in Yorba Linda, a city of about 68,000 people that is part of the Los Angeles metropolitan area. Although no sale price was identified in property records, online real estate portals value the property at roughly $5 million.

Luo was born in China and acquired passports from Cambodia, Vanuatu and Cyprus, according to information from sanctions notices as well as immigration records obtained by OCCRP.

title: Bird Flu Is Raging on a Mink Farm. It Could Spark a Human Pandemic, Experts Say, but Officials Won’t Act.
content:
The strain of bird flu that’s ripped through American barns for the last four years has killed two people who caught it from sick animals. But as far as anyone can tell, humans can’t spread it. The virus has remained a true “bird” flu, tailored to attach to avian cells, not invade human throats and noses, where coughing and sneezing reliably spew droplets. 

Under the right conditions, however, that could change. A single mutation could give the bird flu a foothold in people and spark a pandemic that experts fear could be deadlier than COVID-19. 

For that to happen, this bird flu would likely need to find an intermediate host — an animal vulnerable to viruses that infect both birds and humans. These animals would be crowded together, each infection raising the odds that a new strain could arise through mutation. Then, for that strain to jump across species, it would have to have access to humans and time to spread among them undetected.

title: Europe’s satellite merger tests drive for space independence
content:
BRUSSELS — The EU faces a strategic dilemma over a proposed space merger that has been hailed as a potential European “champion” by Ursula von der Leyen, but could raise costs as the bloc builds out its own secure satellite communications.

The deal between Airbus, Leonardo and Thales would combine their satellite and space systems operations into a business with €6.5 billion in annual sales and 25,000 employees across Europe. 

The EU’s top satellite suppliers say that by joining forces they’ll be able to boost the bloc’s strategic autonomy in space. The three-way alliance, code-named “Bromo,” would not compete directly with Elon Musk’s Starlink, but aims to build Europe’s position in the same fast-growing low Earth orbit satellite market. 

The merger complements the EU’s broader push for strategic autonomy in space based on secure communications for governments and emergency services. The importance of that effort was underscored last week when Ukraine said Starlink’s military-grade service, Starshield, had been throttled at Musk’s initiative, hindering Ukrainian drone operators from intercepting incoming Russian air strikes.

title: Is a job guarantee the solution to mass AI unemployment?
content:
An old idea springs anew as a chorus of influential voices predicts that AI may trigger crises of vast magnitude

In a preface to his book Capitalism and Freedom, the American economist Milton Friedman famously observed that a crisis can propel once-fringe ideas into the political mainstream.

“Only a crisis – actual or perceived – produces real change. When that crisis occurs, the actions that are taken depend on the ideas that are lying around,” he wrote. The job of intellectuals, thinktanks and economists, he argued, is to refine the quality of these ambient ideas, so that good ones are ready when disaster strikes.

title: For Andy Burnham, getting closer to the EU could prove as tricky as exiting it – an expert explains
content:
Andy Burnham has reopened a debate that successive UK prime ministers tried to settle. But the history of Brexit suggests that getting closer to the European Union may prove just as difficult as leaving it.

For years, prime ministers have attempted to put Brexit behind them. Burnham has just done the opposite. By suggesting that Britain could “go all the way” and rejoin the EU, he has broken with the cautious approach of his predecessors.

His intervention has brought renewed urgency to the question: how close should Britain remain to the EU, and on what terms?

The options are not new. From Theresa May’s attempts to secure a bespoke deal to Boris Johnson’s hard Brexit, Rishi Sunak’s pragmatism and Keir Starmer’s reset, governments have grappled with essentially the same dilemma. That is, how can the country retain the benefits of cooperation with the EU without accepting the obligations that come with it?

title: US Court Orders Lebanese Ex-Minister to Pay $35M in Torture and Fraud Case
content:
A U.S. district court has ruled against four Lebanese individuals, including a former minister, finding them liable for fraud, torture and civil conspiracy and ordering them to pay $35 million in damages, for orchestrating the kidnapping and torture of a Lebanese-American couple.

Speaking to OCCRP about the verdict from the Florida court, Lara Samaha, a U.S. green card holder, said the couple filed in the U.S. because “the justice system in Lebanon is so corrupt it is impossible to obtain justice.”

According to the default final judgment seen by OCCRP, a binding court order issued when defendants fail to respond to a lawsuit, the court ordered Gebran Bassil—a sitting member of parliament, Lebanon’s former foreign minister, and the son-in-law of former President Michel Aoun—to pay millions in damages, along with three co-defendants.

“⁠I feel justice has been served after 7 years in court and more than 300 court filings,” Lara Samaha told OCCRP. She confirmed that there will be a follow up on a related lawsuit in Lebanon, though she declined to detail the next steps.

title: Cambodia Cracked Down on Banks Allegedly Linked to Cyber-Scams. The IMF Says the Problem Persists.
content:
Amid mounting international pressure to clean up its financial system, Cambodia’s central bank published a statement earlier this month accusing unnamed actors of waging a campaign of “economic sabotage” against the country.

“Rumors and unverified information have been circulating on social media, claiming that a number of banking and financial institutions are facing issues or heading toward collapse in the near future,” the National Bank of Cambodia (NBC) said.

The NBC did not clarify who might be behind such a campaign, or which institutions were targeted. But the regulator warned that such “baseless” information could undermine “trust in the overall banking system.”

The banking system has taken a beating recently, as international attention turned to Cambodia’s role as a major hub for cyber-scams targeting victims around the world. Proceeds from scams have allegedly flooded into financial institutions.

title: Can LLMs Supercharge Geolocations? Our Tests Show Big Improvements But Humans Remain Key
content:
Sign up here to receive Bellingcat’s biggest investigations by email as soon as they are published.

In September, the AI company Anthropic published a blog post that claimed its models were approaching “superhuman capabilities for geolocating outdoor photos”. Anthropic made this claim by comparing its models’ performance to that of players of the popular online game GeoGuessr, which challenges users to geolocate Google Street View images. 

Bellingcat has been running its own benchmark tests on AI models since June 2025, right around the time when Large Language Models (LLMs) began to challenge reverse image searches for assisting with geolocation tasks. In our first round, GPT 4o-mini from OpenAI appeared to be the best tool for geolocating, a title which was taken by Google AI mode when we performed our second round of tests a few months later in August 2025.

title: Experts: How are climate scientists using artificial intelligence?
content:
Artificial intelligence (AI) is developing at a rapid pace and is increasingly being used by scientists to better understand climate change.

AI is perhaps best-known for its use in “large language models”, such as ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini.

However, the field is vast. 

From weather forecasting to analysing satellite images, climate scientists are using various types of AI to develop faster and more efficient ways to study the warming planet. 

However, the technology comes with no shortage of risks and challenges, including overreliance on unverified results, intensive energy use and exacerbating existing inequalities in climate science.

Carbon Brief spoke to 10 experts working across a range of climate-related fields – from developing climate forecasts to analysing changes in the energy grid – about how AI is being used.

Their answers are set out below, grouped by theme.

  • What are the benefits and challenges of using AI in weather and climate forecasting?
  • What are some other current uses of AI in climate science research?
  • How is AI being used to advance climate policy and action?
  • How could AI be used in climate research over the coming years?

title: Six years on from her unjust imprisonment: Freedom for Kenia Now!
content:
October 18th marked six years since lawyer, feminist and Amuzga indigenous woman human rights defender, Kenia Inés Hernández Montalván, was arbitrarily detained, criminalised and unjustly sentenced to a total of more than 20 years in prison on eleven charges.

Kenia is an Amuzga woman and defender of land, territory, the rights of indigenous peoples and women’s rights. She is the Coordinator of the Zapata Vive Libertarian Collective, which promotes different forms of peaceful resistance against the implementation of capitalist development models.

The reason for her imprisonment? Exercising her legitimate right to protest and to defend human rights. Six years later, despite the fact that in April 2026 she was cleared of the eight federal charges against her, and despite warnings regarding the injustice of her case, from international organisations, human rights bodies and mechanisms, including the IACHR, the UN, as well as Mexican and European parliamentarians, Kenia remains in detention.

title: "A Spark from the Cockroaches": Arundhati Roy on India's Youth Protests & Modi's Crackdown
content:
A court in India on Wednesday ordered the release of two leaders of the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth-led movement that has led historic waves of protests in India since the summer. Ashutosh Ranka and Saurav Das were detained amid massive protests last week after they scaled a barricade to enter a site popular for protest, unfurled the national flag and called for the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. Kumar oversaw the deletion of 130 million names from the voter rolls in India since June of last year. Opposition parties say those impacted are primarily Muslims and other minorities less likely to support the BJP, the Hindu nationalist ruling party of Prime Minister Narendra Modi.

“You have a deep and wide — an ideologically wide — historical culture of resistance in India,” says acclaimed writer and activist Arundhati Roy. At the same time, the Modi government “has three things in its playbook: One is false-flag attacks, two is engineering communal riots, and the third is massive repression. And I don’t think we’ve seen its hand yet.”

title: ECHOES at the NEMO European Museum Conference
content:
Last week, ECHOES partners attended the NEMO European Museum Conference entitled Human after all – Museums in the wake of AI in Vilnius (11th-13th October), Lithuania, and organised a workshop dedicated to Nordic and Baltic cultural heritage professionals on the 14th October. This session invited museum professionals, researchers and policy makers to present their national and regional landscapes, and explore new opportunities for knowledge exchange and collaboration in a complex political and technological context.

During the first half of the workshop, the audience was introduced to the ECHOES project and the Cloud, including detailed presentations of the community engagement activities by FSP and a demonstration of the Cloud’s features and infrastructure design by PCSS. The second half of the session was dedicated to a round table gathering museum professionals from Northen Europe. They were invited to present their national cultural and policy landscape and discuss how the Cloud could support better collaboration beyond national and regional frameworks.

An important output from the NEMO Conference was their statement on AI and Museums, download the PDF here.

title: Juhlavuoden infografiikat esittelivät laitoksen kehitystä
content:
Etlan juhlavuoden kunniaksi julkaistiin kolme infograafia laitoksen kehityksestä vuosien varrella. Infografiikat julkaistiin Etlan Instagram-tilillä ja nyt ne ovat nähtävillä myös tässä uutisessa.

Ensimmäisessä infograafissa sukellettiin Etlan toimitusjohtajien historiaan. Etlalla on ollut yhteensä 13 eri toimitusjohtajaa, joista yksi on toiminut tehtävässä kahdessa eri otteessa. Saat kuvat suuremmaksi klikkaamalla.

Toisessa osassa tarkasteltiin henkilöstön, muistioiden ja raporttien määrää vuosina 2012–2025 välisenä aikana. Vuonna 2025 Etla julkaisi 57 raporttia, muistiota, työpaperia, kirjaa ja ennustetta. Erityisesti muistioiden määrä on kasvanut viime vuosina, ja ne tuovat tutkimustiedon nopeasti ajankohtaiseen keskusteluun.

Mediajulkisuuden määrää esiteltiin puolestaan alla olevassa infograafissa. Etla näkyi mediassa viime vuonna yli 2500 kertaa.

Viimeisenä sukellettiin hieman kevyemmän sisällön dataan. Taloustutkimus on tarkkaa työtä, ja nesteytys kuuluu asiaan. Vuoden 2025 aikana Etlassa juotiin 10 780 kupillista kahvia, 4 422 pulloa kivennäisvettä ja 2 442 pulloa lähdevettä. Yhteensä siis yli 17 600 kuppia ja pulloa.

title: UNICEFin analyysi: Suomen kehitysyhteistyörahoitus vähenee, eikä humanitaarinen apu kohdennu lapsille
content:
Suomen virallinen kehitysapu on vähentynyt noin 23 prosenttia vuoden 2022 tasosta. Kehitysrahoituksen suunta on kansainvälisestikin laskeva, monet suuret rahoittajamaat kuten Yhdysvallat, Iso-Britannia, Ranska ja Saksa ovat leikanneet avustuksiaan.

UNICEFin tuottaman analyysin mukaan Suomen kehitysavusta viidennes kohdistuu lapsille. Kansainvälisesti vertailtuna Suomen prosentti on melko korkea, euromääräisesti kuitenkin vähäinen. Suomen valtion humanitaarisesta rahoituksesta lapsille kohdistuu vain 14 prosenttia.

– Lapset muodostavat kolmanneksen maailman väestöstä ja he kärsivät kriiseissä ja konflikteissa kaikkein eniten. Tästä huolimatta Suomi kohdistaa humanitaarisesta rahoituksestaan vain 14 prosenttia lapsille, kun luku on muissa Pohjoismaissa vähintään kaksinkertainen, sanoo Suomen UNICEFin lapsen oikeuksien ja kehityspolitiikan erityisasiantuntija Mirkka Mattila.

Suomen koulutus- ja terveysrahoituksesta suurin osa menee lapsille. Rahoituksen kehitys on kuitenkin laskeva. Lapsiin kohdistuva koulutusrahoitus on vähentynyt 57 prosenttia vuoden 2021 huipputasosta.

title: Lessons from Maricarmen
content:
The case of Maricarmen Abascal, an 87-year-old woman from Madrid who passed away just days after being evicted from the apartment where she had lived – and for which she had paid – for decades, has resonated far beyond Spain’s borders. It has become a powerful symbol of a deeper crisis affecting our societies. For too long, housing has been treated primarily as a commodity rather than as a fundamental human right. For too long, we have been told that markets would regulate themselves and that public intervention would do more harm than good. Today, the evidence is undeniable: that approach has failed.

The question we must now confront is straightforward: what must we do to ensure that housing is guaranteed as a right, and not merely traded as an asset?

title: TNR Watch: The Enduring Problem of Transnational Repression in Southeast Asia
content:
Déjà vu: Two apparent incidents of transnational repression (TNR) endangered several diaspora activists in Southeast Asia in mid-September. On September 15, Khieo Lapchanh, a Thailand-based Laotian asylum seeker known for his online criticism of Laos’s government, went missing outside Bangkok. The 26-year-old, who was set to attend an asylum interview at the UN Refugee agency office in Bangkok a day later, reportedly was the target of an $8,000 bounty circulating online.

Three days after Lapchanh’s disappearance, three Vietnamese activists—Nguyen Duc Thuan, Ho Pham Hiep Huy, and Thai Cong Truong Son—were abducted from Cambodia and returned to Vietnam, where they are under investigation for “terrorism” and forging documents. Australian resident Hiep and dual Norwegian-Vietnamese citizen Thuan went to Cambodia to meet and train other Vietnamese human rights defenders. According to the prodemocracy organization Viet Tan, which Hiep and Thuan belong to, Vietnamese authorities initially prevented consular visits by Australian and Norwegian representatives to the two while they were in detention.

title: What telecoms leave behind when they exit a country
content:
When telecoms pull out of markets, data protection and human rights commitments often disappear

Originally published on Global Voices Advox

Image by Akil Mazumder via Pexels. Used under a Pexels license.

By Jie Zhang 

This post is part of Global Voices’ October 2026 Spotlight series, “Big Tech and Authoritarianism.” In this Spotlight, we explore how Big Tech facilitates and hinders authoritarian governments and practices, and how these choices influence the Global South. You can support this coverage by donating here.

In March 2022, just over a year after Myanmar’s military coup, Telenor, the Norwegian telecommunications giant, sold its subsidiary in the country to M1 Group, bringing nearly eight years of operation to an end. But leaving Myanmar did not end the controversy surrounding its departure. Instead, the hasty exit came back to haunt the company over the next four years.
